dimension: Canvas interaction and network manipulation (NetworkCanvasView / ScrollContainer / Layers / Overlays / CanvasGeometry / ToolPaletteView / NetworkEditorModel / keyboard)

already_good.what: Alignment guides are genuinely commercial-grade. `SmartGuides.match` tests all three x-guides and all three y-guides (minX/midX/maxX, minY/midY/maxY) of the dragged node's world rect against every other node's rect, AND falls back to an equal-spacing match ("the two nearest neighbours in the same row/column") when no edge matches. The drag then arbitrates PER AXIS between the guide and Snap to Grid, whichever is nearer, and ⌃ held live suspends both. This is Figma/Sketch behaviour, and it is already here. Do not rebuild it.
already_good.evidence: Sources/Qnet/CanvasGeometry.swift:1184-1330 (Match, tolerance=4, guides(), match(), spacing()); Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasView.swift:558-611 (per-axis grid-vs-guide arbitration); Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasView.swift:613-621 (⌃ read live, not at mouse-down); Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasLayers.swift:68 (AlignmentGuideLayer)

already_good.what: Marquee selection follows the OmniGraffle/Figma intersection rule (a node the band *touches* is selected, not only one whose centre is inside), with a live preview highlight on every candidate node and a live count in the status bar — and all three read the SAME predicate `CanvasScene.marqueeSelects`, so what lights up is exactly what commits. ⇧-drag unions with the existing selection.

⌥-drag duplicate-and-move is implemented end to end and correctly: ⌥ at mouse-down is captured by an AppKit local monitor *before* SwiftUI's gesture runs, the copies are made in place inside the already-open undo group so "Duplicate and Move Nodes" is ONE undo step, the drag re-anchors onto the copies, and the `.dragCopy` cursor previews it while ⌥ is held over a node.

Arrow-key nudge is coalesced into one undo entry per key-run (a held arrow at ~15 Hz does not produce 15 undo steps), the run closes on key-up, on selection change, on a new mutation, or on timeout; the step is one whole grid cell while Snap to Grid is on so an arrow can never knock a snapped node off the grid; and the group moves rigidly by the anchor's snapped delta rather than re-snapping each member (which would collapse a hand-made layout).
already_good.evidence: Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:1793-1875 (nudgeSelection, endNudgeRun, nudgeStep); Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasScrollContainer.swift:625-631, 696-708, 712-720 (keyUp / resignFirstResponder close the run)

already_good.what: The cursor has exactly one owner and no push/pop pairs anywhere — a cursor rect on the clip view, recomputed from a pure `cursorForCurrentState()` whenever tool / hover / drag / space-pan publishes. This is the correct architecture and it means a future sticky-pan mode needs NO cursor work at all: setting `selectedTool = .pan` already flips the cursor to `.openHand` through the existing Combine subscription.

Pan/zoom gesture coverage on the AppKit side is already close to complete: plain two-finger scroll pans in every tool, ⌥/⌘+wheel zooms geometrically about the pointer, trackpad pinch zooms about the pointer, two-finger double-tap (smartMagnify) fits the selection or the whole network, middle-button drag pans without changing the tool, and Space held pans in every tool. All clamp to one `zoomRange` (0.1–4.0).

Keyboard reachability of every object: Tab / ⇧Tab walk nodes in reading order and ⌥Tab / ⌥⇧Tab walk the links attached to the selected node, each scrolling the target into view only when it is actually off-screen (88 pt margin covering the label block). Links also publish one VoiceOver element each, positioned on their label anchor, with Edit Parameters and Delete Link actions — dropped only during the two frame-rate interactions.

Undo/redo is snapshot-based over the full structural state (nodes, links, infiniteBuffers, all four name counters), unlimited depth, correctly round-trips ⌘Z→⇧⌘Z by re-registering the reverse transition, preserves the selection across undo so the docked Inspector shows the restored value, and drops only ids the restored snapshot no longer contains. `beginMutation`/`endMutation` ignore nested begins and skip registration when nothing structural changed.

Rendering correctness under interaction: one memoised `CanvasScene` feeds the grid, links, nodes, marquee, every hit test and the right-click hit test, so what is drawn is exactly what is hit at any zoom/pan; the link route plan is frozen for the duration of a node drag (so arrows don't snap between bulge rungs mid-drag) and eased between generations on release instead of teleporting.

The canvas status bar is a real commercial status bar: active tool with its icon, zoom percentage, live selection summary (nodes + link) that agrees exactly with Deselect All's enablement, primitive counts that degrade from words to symbols via ViewThatFits, snap state with a distinct "Free placement" readout while ⌃ is held, buffer regime, and a pan-offset segment that appears only when panned. Every tooltip cites its key through `KeyboardShortcutReference.key(for:)` rather than a hard-coded glyph.

Tool hotkeys V M H S B O X L match the Figma/OmniGraffle set, come from one source of truth (`EditorTool(shortcutCharacter:)`) shared by the canvas key handler, the Tools menu and the palette badges, and `ToolShortcutGuard` stops those bare letters being stolen from text fields, sheets and the embedded terminal by AppKit's menu key-equivalent matching.

Link probability chips declutter properly: below a scale threshold none are drawn, above it the selected and hovered links reserve their chip rect first so they always win, and other chips are dropped when they would overlap — so a dense routing graph stays readable and hovering is the documented way to recover a dropped label.

Scrollers are real: `CanvasScrollMetrics` is a pure function of nodes + transform, expresses drag targets in pan space (`panAt0X`/`panAt1X`) so the mapping is stable while the knob is dragged, deliberately does not snap the pan back when overflow disappears, and the three geometry publishers are merged and throttled to ~16 ms so a node drag cannot cause one scroller refresh per publish.

findings.title: Make Delete remove a selected link
findings.user_impact: Select a link (click it), press Delete or ⌫ — nothing happens, and no message is printed. The Edit ▸ Delete menu item is *enabled* in that state, so the user gets a dead command with no feedback. The only working ways to delete a link are the right-click menu or Edit ▸ Delete Selected Link, which carries no key equivalent. For a tool whose whole document is a routing graph, being unable to delete an arc with the Delete key is the single most damaging canvas defect present.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:680-682 — `deleteSelection()` computes `currentSelectionIDs()` (nodes only, NetworkEditorModel.swift:697-701) and `guard !ids.isEmpty else { return }`, so a link-only selection returns immediately. Sources/Qnet/QnetCommands.swift:147 `hasSelection = hasNodeSelection || editor.selectedLinkID != nil` gates the menu item at Sources/Qnet/QnetCommands.swift:414-418, so the item is enabled. Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasScrollContainer.swift:604-605 routes keyCodes 51/117 to the same dead call. Sources/Qnet/QnetCommands.swift:421-426 is the working-but-unbound "Delete Selected Link".
findings.proposed_fix: In `NetworkEditorModel.deleteSelection()` handle the link case: capture `selectedLinkID` alongside `ids`, change the guard to `guard !ids.isEmpty || selectedLinkID != nil else { return }`, and inside the existing `performMutation("Delete")` block remove `links.removeAll { $0.id == linkID }` before the node removal. Name the undo step by what was removed ("Delete Link" / "Delete" / "Delete Selection") so the Edit menu reads correctly. Make the status line say what was deleted, matching `deleteLink`'s wording at NetworkEditorModel.swift:590-598. Leave `deleteLink(id:)` alone — the context menu and VoiceOver action use it.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Click a link so the status bar reads "Selected 1 link"; press Delete. The link disappears, the status log gains one "Deleted link …" line, and ⌘Z restores it in one step. Repeat with a mixed selection (2 nodes + 1 link): all three go in one undo step. `swift build` and validation/design_lint.sh still pass; no gui_runtime_contracts.sh string is touched (that script only greps QnetGUIApp.swift / SRBMExporter.swift / ctmc_dtandem.py — see validation/gui_runtime_contracts.sh:7-9).
findings.risk: `deleteSelection` is also called from `cutSelection` (NetworkEditorModel.swift:616-628), which currently guards on node ids being non-empty; a link-only Cut would now delete the link without having copied it, because `copySelection` only copies nodes. Guard Cut to keep its current node-only semantics, or make the clipboard link-aware in the same change.

findings.title: Allow drawing a self-loop (station-to-itself feedback arc)
findings.user_impact: Qnet is a queueing-network tool whose solvers, warnings and help text all speak about self-loops (P[i][i] > 0), and whose renderer already draws them as a nested arc above the node — but the Link tool flatly refuses to create one, printing "Cannot link a node to itself." A user cannot draw the single most common reentrant primitive (rework / retry at a station) on the canvas at all. They must hand-edit a .bnet file, use the AI assistant's `add_link` (which has no such guard), or generate a random reentrant network.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:1982-1986 — `if startID == nodeID { addStatus("Cannot link a node to itself."); return }`. Rendering support already exists: Sources/Qnet/CanvasGeometry.swift:343-370 `LinkGeometry.selfLoop(...)` with `extraRadius` so multi-class loops nest, dispatched at Sources/Qnet/CanvasGeometry.swift:1059-1061 on `link.fromNodeID == link.toNodeID`. Export/diagnostics support exists: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:6566-6569 lists self-loop stations, QnetGUIApp.swift:7053 reports max P[i][i], QnetGUIApp.swift:6807 handles P[i][i] ≥ 1. Sources/Qnet/CanvasImageExport.swift:131 pads for a self-loop chip. The AI path has no guard: Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:2124-2148 `addLink(fromID:toID:)`.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the blanket refusal at NetworkEditorModel.swift:1982-1986 with a kind-aware rule: allow `startID == nodeID` when the node is a `.station` (and `.buffer` if the semantics permit), reject it for `.source` and `.sink` with a message that says *why* ("A source has no service to repeat"). Route the allowed case through the existing class-selection logic below it (candidateClasses / usedClasses / chosenClass) so a multi-class self-loop picks a free class exactly as a normal link does, and keep the chain-continuation behaviour. Second click on the SAME node is currently how the user would express it, which conflicts with nothing else in the addLink flow.
findings.acceptance_criteria: With the Link tool, click station S1 twice: an arc appears above S1 with its probability chip, `linkDescription` reads "S1 → S1", Network ▸ Analyze Network reports it under self-loops, ⌘Z removes it, and the diagram export (Copy as Image) includes it. Clicking a source twice still refuses, with a message naming the reason. `validation/canvas_perf/run_routing_check.sh` still passes.
findings.risk: Exporters must tolerate a diagonal routing entry. Several already do (QnetGUIApp.swift:6566, 6807), but BNASRBMExporter's reachability walks (Sources/Qnet/BNASRBMExporter.swift:990, 1017) and the traffic-equation solve behind `refreshStationUtilisation` (NetworkEditorModel.swift:1645-1668) should be checked for an infinite loop or singular matrix at P[i][i] → 1 before this ships. The FlagBar feedback classifier (NetworkEditorModel.swift:210-235) already has a self-loop branch.

findings.title: Make drag-from-node-to-node create a link, and show an elastic preview line
findings.user_impact: Drag-to-connect is the universal way to draw an arc in Visio, OmniGraffle, Simulink, yEd and Figma. Here it is a silent no-op: with the Link tool active, pressing on S1, dragging to S2 and releasing sets the *start* to S1 and nothing else — the user has released the mouse over the target and got no link, no error, and no explanation. Even the two-click flow they must fall back on gives no elastic rubber-band line from the start node to the pointer; the only feedback is a static dashed ring on the start node plus a status-log line, so the user cannot see what they are about to connect.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasView.swift:466-470 — `nodeDrag`'s `onChanged` returns immediately unless the tool is `.select` or `.multiSelect`, so `dragNodeID` stays nil. Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasView.swift:658-661 — the canvas-level drag returns for `.node` origins. Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasView.swift:508-530 — `onEnded` therefore takes the plain-click path and calls `handleNodeTap` with the *press* node, reaching `handleLinkSelection` (NetworkEditorModel.swift:1963-1980) which only records the start. The release target is never consulted. Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasView.swift:319-339 `pendingLinkIndicator` draws only a dashed outline around the start node — there is no path to the pointer anywhere in the layer stack (Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasLayers.swift:149-311 draws only committed links). Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasLayers.swift:419-421 documents that nodes deliberately have no handles.
findings.proposed_fix: Two parts. (1) Drag-to-connect: in `nodeDrag.onChanged`, add an `.addLink` branch that records `pendingLinkStartID = node.id` once the drag threshold is crossed and publishes the live pointer position into a new `@Published var pendingLinkPoint: CGPoint?` on the editor; in `nodeDrag.onEnded`, when a link drag is in flight, hit-test the release location against `scene.hitNode(at:)` and call the existing `handleLinkSelection(targetID)` so the class-selection and duplicate-pair rules are unchanged; release on empty canvas cancels. (2) Elastic preview: extend `pendingLinkIndicator` to stroke a dashed path from the start node's boundary to `pendingLinkPoint` (or to the hovered node's boundary when one is under the pointer) using the same `chainColor` it already computes, `allowsHitTesting(false)` and `accessibilityHidden(true)`. Feed `pendingLinkPoint` from the existing `updateHover` tracker (NetworkCanvasView.swift:434-461) so the two-click flow gets the same preview with no extra event plumbing. All strokes must use DS tokens — the existing code at NetworkCanvasView.swift:330-334 shows the sanctioned `max(1.5, 2 * s)` / dash pattern shape.
findings.acceptance_criteria: With the Link tool: press on S1, drag — a dashed accent line follows the pointer; hover S2 — the line snaps to S2's boundary and S2 shows its hover ring; release — the link is created and the status log prints the same "Linked …" line the two-click flow prints. Releasing on empty canvas leaves no link and clears the preview. The two-click flow also shows the elastic line while a start node is pending. Escape cancels. design_lint.sh passes (no raw colours, no literal stroke widths outside the DS spellings already used in this file).
findings.risk: The node's `DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)` and the canvas-level drag both fire; the `.node` early-return at NetworkCanvasView.swift:658-661 must keep the canvas gesture out of the way. Publishing `pendingLinkPoint` on every drag frame adds an editor publish per frame — route it through the existing hover path, which is already throttled by `onContinuousHover`, and confirm against validation/canvas_perf/run_canvas_bench.sh that the per-frame budget documented in CanvasGeometry.swift's CanvasProfiler comment is unchanged.

findings.title: Add the sticky pan mode the user asked for: double-click empty canvas → hand, single click → pointer
findings.user_impact: The user named this explicitly. Today a double-click on empty canvas does nothing at all in the Pointer tool (two deselects), and in an add tool it silently places TWO nodes at the same snapped grid point — the second sitting exactly under the first, invisible, and quietly corrupting the network. Sticky panning exists only via the H key or the palette, and there is no way back to the pointer except V or the palette; nothing on the canvas surface teaches either.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasView.swift:744-749 — the empty-canvas `onEnded` has no double-click branch at all; it calls `editor.handleCanvasTap` unconditionally. Contrast with the node path at NetworkCanvasView.swift:517-528 and the link path at NetworkCanvasView.swift:721-728, which BOTH implement double-click via `lastNodeTapTime` / `lastLinkTapTime` against `NSEvent.doubleClickInterval` (NetworkCanvasView.swift:177-180, 191) — so the pattern to copy is already in this file. `handleCanvasTap` (NetworkEditorModel.swift:402-425) places a node on every tap for the four add tools, hence the double placement. The current no-tool-change rule is a deliberate documented decision at NetworkCanvasView.swift:39-40 and NetworkCanvasView.swift:768-770, so this is a reversal, not an omission. There is no previous-tool memory anywhere (grep for previousTool/toolBefore/lastTool returns nothing).
findings.proposed_fix: Mirror the node/link double-click machinery: add `@State private var lastCanvasTapTime: Date` and `lastCanvasTapPoint: CGPoint?` to `CanvasContentView`. In the empty-canvas `onEnded` branch, when the tool is `.select` or `.multiSelect` and the second click lands within `Self.doubleClickInterval` and a few points of the first, call a new `editor.enterStickyPan()` instead of `handleCanvasTap`; that method stores the outgoing tool in a new `@Published private(set) var toolBeforeStickyPan: EditorTool?` and calls `setTool(.pan)`. In the `.pan` branch of `handleCanvasTap`, if `toolBeforeStickyPan != nil`, restore that tool and clear the memo — that is the "single click returns to pointer" half, and it costs nothing because a Pan-tool click already routes there (NetworkEditorModel.swift:412-418). Separately, suppress the second placement in the add tools by requiring the tap to be outside the double-click window OR at a different snapped point. Crucially: the cursor needs NO work. The clip view is the sole cursor owner and already subscribes to `$selectedTool` (NetworkCanvasScrollContainer.swift:172-184), and `cursorForCurrentState()` already returns `.openHand` for `.pan` and `.closedHand` while `isPanningCanvas` (NetworkCanvasScrollContainer.swift:731-751), so setting the tool flips the hand automatically with no push/pop and no new cursor rect. Update the doc comments at NetworkCanvasView.swift:39-40 and :768-770 (they currently assert the opposite) and add the gesture to `KeyboardShortcutReference.unprintedKeys` (KeyboardShortcutReference.swift:139-151) so it appears in Help ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Pointer tool, double-click empty canvas: the cursor becomes an open hand, the status bar's tool segment reads "Pan", and dragging pans. A single click anywhere returns the tool to Pointer and the cursor to the arrow. H and the palette still work and are unaffected by the memo. With the Station tool, a fast double-click on empty canvas places exactly ONE station (verified by the status-bar primitive count). The gesture is listed under "KEYS NOT PRINTED IN A MENU" in Help ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts. design_lint.sh and swift build pass.
findings.risk: The first click of the double-click already cleared the selection and the class filter (NetworkEditorModel.swift:412-419); that is acceptable but should be conscious. The marquee threshold (NetworkCanvasView.swift:198, 5 pt) means a slightly-moved second click becomes a rubber-band instead — require the double-click points to be within ~3 pt. `setTool(.pan)` calls `clearMultiSelection()` (NetworkEditorModel.swift:394-396), which is correct here but means entering sticky pan drops a marquee group; restore-on-exit does not bring it back.

findings.title: Let an existing link be re-targeted; stop "dragging a link" silently moving both its nodes
findings.user_impact: There is no way to change where an arc goes. A user who drew S1 → S3 and meant S1 → S2 must delete the link and redraw it, losing its routing probability, customer class and exit-class transition. Worse, the gesture a diagram user would reach for — grabbing the arc and dragging — does something completely different and destructive-looking: it translates BOTH endpoint nodes across the canvas, silently rearranging the layout. There are also no bend points or waypoints, so a route the auto-router bows the wrong way around an obstacle cannot be corrected by hand.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/Models.swift:979-980 — `let fromNodeID: UUID` and `let toNodeID: UUID` are immutable, so no re-target API can exist; grep confirms nothing assigns them. Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasView.swift:663-684 — a drag on a link opens `beginMutation("Move Link")` and calls `moveAnchoredNodes` on `[from.id, to.id]`, i.e. it moves the two stations. Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:550-565 `moveLink` does the same. Routing is fully automatic with no user input: Sources/Qnet/CanvasGeometry.swift:689-696 `LinkRoutePlan` stores only a scalar bulge per link id, built solely from node geometry (NetworkEditorModel.swift:1618-1636). The only per-link edits offered are class, exit class, probability and delete (Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasView.swift:817-862).
findings.proposed_fix: Two independent pieces, in this order. (1) Re-target: make `fromNodeID`/`toNodeID` `var` on `NetworkLink` and add `editor.retargetLink(id:newFrom:newTo:)` inside `performMutation("Reconnect Link")`, re-running the same class-availability check `handleLinkSelection` uses (NetworkEditorModel.swift:1993-2020) so a re-target cannot create a duplicate (pair, class). Surface it as endpoint handles: when a link is selected, draw two small DS-styled grips at `geometry.start` and `geometry.tip`; dragging a grip shows the elastic preview from finding #3 and drops on the node under the pointer. (2) Change what a plain link-body drag does: either make it a no-op that only selects (safest), or reserve it for a future waypoint. Do NOT keep "drag the arc, move two stations" — no commercial canvas does that, and the current undo name "Move Link" describes something the user did not ask for.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Select S1 → S3; two grips appear at its ends. Drag the head grip onto S2; the arc now reads S1 → S2, its routing probability and customer class are unchanged, the Inspector shows the same link object, and ⌘Z restores S1 → S3 in one step. Dragging onto a node that would duplicate an existing (pair, class) refuses with the same message `handleLinkSelection` prints. Dragging the link body no longer moves any node. Round-trip through .bnet save/load preserves the retargeted link (Models.swift Codable keys are unchanged).
findings.risk: `NetworkLink` is `Hashable`/`Codable` and is compared by value in the scene cache key (NetworkCanvasView.swift:118) and the route-plan cache (NetworkEditorModel.swift:1620-1636); making the endpoints mutable does not change that, but every `links.firstIndex(where:)` mutation path must go through `performMutation` or undo will miss it. Removing the "drag link moves nodes" behaviour changes a documented gesture (NetworkCanvasView.swift:35) — update that comment and the drag-origin switch together.

findings.title: Support multi-link selection (marquee, ⇧-click, Select All)
findings.user_impact: Exactly one link can be selected at a time, and the marquee never selects links at all. A user cannot rubber-band a sub-chain and delete it with its arcs, cannot select five arcs and set them all to Class 2, and cannot ⌘A a routing graph and see the links included. In a tool whose document is mostly arcs, every link operation is one-at-a-time.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:35 — `@Published var selectedLinkID: UUID?` is the entire link-selection model; there is no `selectedLinkIDs`. Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:1446-1473 `finalizeMultiSelect` filters `nodes` only and never touches `links` or `selectedLinkID`. Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:1503-1510 `selectAll()` sets `selectedLinkID = nil` explicitly. Sources/Qnet/ContentView.swift:1099-1106 hard-codes "1 link" in every branch of the selection summary. Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:525-541 `handleLinkTap` has no extending-selection parameter, unlike `handleNodeTap` (NetworkEditorModel.swift:432).
findings.proposed_fix: Introduce `@Published var selectedLinkIDs: Set<UUID>` alongside the existing single id and normalise exactly as `setNodeSelection` does for nodes (one → single id, several → set, none → both cleared; NetworkEditorModel.swift:479-489), so every existing single-link consumer (Inspector, link context menu, Delete Selected Link) keeps working unchanged. Extend `finalizeMultiSelect` to add links whose `geometry` intersects the marquee rect using a world-space version of the existing `LinkGeometry.distance(to:)` (CanvasGeometry.swift:238) — or, simpler and matching Visio, add a link when both its endpoints are enclosed. Give `handleLinkTap` an `extendingSelection` parameter fed from the same `lastMouseDownExtendsSelection` flag the node path uses (NetworkCanvasScrollContainer.swift:455). Update `deleteSelection`, `copySelection` and the status-bar summary to pluralise. Make the link context menu's class pickers apply to the whole link selection when the right-clicked link is in it, exactly as the node context menu already does for align/distribute (NetworkCanvasView.swift:866-876, 910-942).
findings.acceptance_criteria: Rubber-band a sub-chain: the enclosed nodes AND the arcs between them highlight, the status bar reads "Selected 4 nodes, 3 links", Delete removes all seven in one undo step. ⇧-click adds and removes individual arcs. Right-click one of several selected links and set Customer Class — all selected links change in one undo step. The Inspector still shows the single-link editor when exactly one link is selected.
findings.risk: `LinkLayerState` is `Equatable` on `selectedLinkID` (NetworkCanvasLayers.swift:153-160) and drives the link canvas's redraw skip; swapping in a Set changes that equality check and could cost a redraw per frame if done carelessly — keep the Set out of the per-frame state or compare by count+hash. `selectedLinkID` is read in many places (Inspector, QnetCommands.swift:421, flag bar); keeping it as the derived single-selection value avoids touching them.

findings.title: Fit the view after opening a file, an example, or a generated network
findings.user_impact: Opening a bundled example or a colleague's .bnet restores whatever pan and zoom that file was saved with. A network authored on a large display, or one saved while panned away, opens showing empty canvas — the user sees the "No Network Yet" style void, or a corner of a diagram, and must already know ⇧⌘0 to recover. Generate Random Network is worse: at the default 4 stations the layout already reaches x ≈ 760 world pt and at 8 stations x ≈ 1280, well past a typical canvas viewport at 100 %, so a freshly generated network is partly off-screen with no fit and nothing telling the user why.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:1385-1386 — `loadNetwork` assigns `canvasScale = document.canvasScale; canvasPanOffset = document.canvasPanOffset` verbatim; nothing calls `zoomToFit()` afterwards. Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:1379-1418 `loadNetworkFile` calls `showNetworkPrimitives()` but never fits. Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:1157-1177 `createRandomNetworkTab` assigns nodes/links directly and never fits. Sources/Qnet/RandomNetworkGenerator.swift:70-75, 126-129 — `xRowStart = 200`, `xStep = 130`, sink at `200 + d*130 + 40`. `zoomToFit` itself is correct and available (NetworkEditorModel.swift:1566-1586) but its only callers are the menu, the zoom cluster, the context menu and smartMagnify (grep of `zoomToFit()`).
findings.proposed_fix: After `loadNetwork(document:)` completes in `loadNetworkFile` (QnetGUIApp.swift:1391-1407, both the reuse-blank-tab and new-tab branches) and after `createRandomNetworkTab` populates the editor, call `zoomToFit()` — but only once `canvasViewportSize` is non-zero. `fit(nodes:)` already no-ops on a zero viewport (NetworkEditorModel.swift:1578-1582), and `canvasViewportSize` is published by the canvas GeometryReader (NetworkCanvasView.swift:60-63), so the reliable hook is a one-shot `pendingFitOnAppear` flag on the editor that the canvas consumes in its `onChange(of: geometry.size)` / `onAppear`. Preserve the saved transform when it already frames the content: fit only if the content's on-screen bbox is empty or overflows the viewport — `CanvasScrollMetrics.compute` (NetworkCanvasScrollContainer.swift:291-366) already returns exactly the overflow numbers needed for that test, so reuse it rather than writing a second predicate.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Open an example whose saved pan puts it off-screen: the network is fully framed on screen the moment the tab appears, and the zoom readout shows the fitted percentage. Open a file saved at a sensible 100 % view that already fits: the saved zoom/pan is preserved unchanged (verify the zoom readout still says 100 % and the pan segment does not appear). Generate Random Network with 8 stations: the whole chain including Sink1 is visible. Restoring tabs at launch (TabPersistence.swift:82-83) behaves the same way.
findings.risk: QnetGUIApp.swift is the file gui_runtime_contracts.sh greps (validation/gui_runtime_contracts.sh:7), so read that script before editing — none of its patterns touch the load path today, but confirm rather than assume. Fitting must not fire before the canvas has reported a viewport, or the transform is silently left alone and the bug looks intermittent. Do not mark the document dirty: `canvasScale`/`canvasPanOffset` feed TabPersistence's change hook (TabPersistence.swift:128-129) and `markDocumentClean()` runs at the end of `loadNetwork` (NetworkEditorModel.swift:1424).

findings.title: Replace the dead empty-canvas hint with a real starting point: archetype templates
findings.user_impact: The user asked for the canvas to guide network construction from scratch with archetypes. What exists is a static, non-clickable text block that says "Press S, then click to place a station." A new user facing a blank canvas has no way to get a working M/M/1, a K-station tandem, an open Jackson network with feedback, or a reentrant line without knowing the file format, hunting File ▸ Open Example… through an NSOpenPanel, or discovering Network ▸ Generate Random Network… (which is random, replaces the tab, and can't insert into an existing drawing).
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasOverlays.swift:161-170 — `CanvasEmptyHint` is a `DSEmptyState` with `.allowsHitTesting(false)` on the whole thing (NetworkCanvasOverlays.swift:169), so it cannot host an action even though `DSEmptyState` supports one (Sources/Qnet/DSEmptyState.swift:29-31, 80-92). `NetworkCanvasView.swift:76-80` shows it only when `editor.nodes.isEmpty`. No template/archetype machinery exists anywhere (grep for archetype/template across Sources/Qnet returns only unrelated hits). The nearest thing is `RandomNetworkGenerator.Topology` (Sources/Qnet/RandomNetworkGenerator.swift:27-39: feedForward, jacksonFeedback, generalPMatrix, reentrantFeedback), reachable only through Network ▸ Generate Random Network… (QnetCommands.swift:729) which always creates a NEW tab (QnetGUIApp.swift:1167-1176). The tool palette is node-primitive only, with no drag-and-drop (Sources/Qnet/ToolPaletteView.swift:20-37; grep for onDrag/onDrop/draggable finds only tab reordering at ContentView.swift:511-548).
findings.proposed_fix: Add a `NetworkArchetypes` enum owning a handful of named, parameterised structural templates (M/M/1; M/M/c; tandem of K stations; K-station tandem with feedback to station 1; fork-join; reentrant two-class line) that each return `([NetworkNode], [NetworkLink])` laid out on the 28 pt grid relative to an insertion origin — the same shape `RandomNetworkGenerator.Result` already uses (RandomNetworkGenerator.swift:51-57), so the insertion path is `performMutation("Insert <archetype>")` + append + `setNodeSelection(newIDs)` + `zoomToFitSelection()`. Surface it three ways: (a) remove `.allowsHitTesting(false)` from `CanvasEmptyHint` and give the `DSEmptyState` its action button ("Start from a Template…"); (b) a Network ▸ Insert Template ▸ submenu, enabled always so an archetype can be dropped into an existing drawing at the viewport centre; (c) the canvas empty-area context menu (NetworkCanvasView.swift:789-814), which today offers only Paste/Select/Zoom. Each template must produce a network that passes `SRBMExporter.computeData` with ρ < 1 out of the box, so "insert, then Run" works with zero parameter editing — that is what makes it an archetype rather than a shape stamp.
findings.acceptance_criteria: On a blank canvas, the empty state shows a clickable "Start from a Template…" button. Choosing "Tandem (3 stations)" produces Src1 → B1 → S1 → B2 → S2 → B3 → S3 → Sink1 laid out on the grid, framed by an automatic fit, selected as a group, and undoable in ONE step. Network ▸ Analyze Network reports it tractable with ρ < 1 and Run ▸ QNA succeeds without the user editing a single parameter. Inserting a second template into a non-empty canvas offsets it clear of the existing nodes and does not renumber the existing ones (the counters at NetworkEditorModel.swift:2152-2156 must be respected). design_lint.sh passes, including the Title Case rule on any new `DSEmptyState(title:)`.
findings.risk: Node naming must go through the existing counter re-sync used by paste (NetworkEditorModel.swift:2152-2156 / pasteClipboardContents) or an inserted template will collide with existing S1/B1 names and corrupt the export, which resolves stations by name (NetworkEditorModel.swift:336-347). A new `DSEmptyState` action button changes hit-testing on the canvas overlay — confirm a click that misses the button still reaches the canvas gesture beneath (the DSEmptyState text sub-views already set `allowsHitTesting(false)` individually at DSEmptyState.swift:73, 79, which is why the blanket modifier can be dropped).

findings.title: Promote Align and Distribute out of the node context menu into the menu bar, and align by edges not centres
findings.user_impact: Six layout commands exist and work, but they are reachable ONLY by right-clicking a node that is part of a ≥2-node selection. They appear in no menu, no toolbar and no keyboard shortcut, so a user who selects nodes with the marquee and looks in the menu bar concludes the app cannot align. There is also no Align Centre (horizontal or vertical) and no "distribute with equal gaps" — only "distribute centres evenly", which leaves visibly uneven gaps between nodes of different sizes. And Align Top sets every node's centre y to the topmost centre y, so aligning a buffer (44 pt tall) with a station (48 pt) leaves their tops 2 pt apart — inconsistent with the drag-time guides, which align by true edges.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasView.swift:866-876 — the only call sites, gated on `editor.selectedNodeIDs.count >= 2 && contains(node.id)`. Grep of QnetCommands.swift and QnetGUIApp.swift for Align/Distribute finds nothing but `Straighten Network` (QnetCommands.swift:719-725). Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:1689-1745 — all four align helpers operate on `position.y` / `position.x`, i.e. centres. Contrast Sources/Qnet/CanvasGeometry.swift:1230-1232, where the live guides use `[r.minX, r.midX, r.maxX]` of the node's world rect. Node sizes genuinely differ: Sources/Qnet/CanvasGeometry.swift:95-102 (station 48×48, buffer 52×44, source 46×46, sink 48×48). Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:1746-1782 distributes centres, not gaps.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an Arrange section to the Network menu (next to Straighten Network at QnetCommands.swift:719) with Align Left / Centre / Right / Top / Middle / Bottom and Distribute Horizontally / Vertically, each disabled on the same predicate the context menu uses; keep the context menu as a mirror with identical titles, exactly as the Edit Parameters… pattern already does (NetworkCanvasView.swift:818-821). Change the four existing helpers to compute from `CanvasScene.nodeWorldRect($0)` edges (CanvasGeometry.swift:1124-1129) rather than centre coordinates, so a mixed-kind selection lines up the way the drag guides promised it would, and add the two missing centre alignments. Add a gap-equalising distribute alongside the existing centre-equalising one. Do NOT add bare ⌘-digit shortcuts (design_lint forbids them outside the tab commands); if shortcuts are wanted, use ⌃⌘-letter and register them in `KeyboardShortcutReference.Command` with a `menuPath` so `auditTable(against:)` keeps them honest (KeyboardShortcutReference.swift:27-133).
findings.acceptance_criteria: Marquee-select a station and a buffer, choose Network ▸ Arrange ▸ Align Top: their rendered top edges are flush on screen (not their centres). Every Arrange item appears in the menu bar with the same title as its context-menu twin and is dimmed when fewer than 2 (or 3, for distribute) nodes are selected. Each is one undo step. If shortcuts are added, `QNET_MENU_AUDIT=1` reports no duplicate key and `KeyboardShortcutReference.auditTable` reports no drift. design_lint.sh passes (no bare ⌘-digit).
findings.risk: Switching from centres to edges changes the result of existing align commands, so any saved layout a user re-aligns will shift slightly — acceptable and correct, but call it out in the changelog. The align helpers guard on `selectedNodeIDs.count >= 2`, and `setNodeSelection` collapses a single-node group into `selectedNodeID` (NetworkEditorModel.swift:479-489); the new menu items must gate on `selectionUnion.count`, not `selectedNodeIDs.count`, or they will be wrongly dimmed.

findings.title: Add graph-aware selection: Select Connected, Select Upstream/Downstream, Invert Selection, Select by Kind
findings.user_impact: On a 40-node network there is no way to grab a sub-network. To select one chain the user must rubber-band it geometrically and hope the layout cooperates, or ⇧-click every node. There is no Invert Selection, no "select everything reachable from here", and no "select all stations". For a tool whose document is a directed graph and whose users routinely want to operate on a branch, this is the largest structural selection gap.
findings.evidence: Grep across Sources/Qnet for selectConnected / Select Connected / invertSelection / Invert Selection / selectDownstream returns nothing. The entire selection vocabulary is: `selectAll` (NetworkEditorModel.swift:1503-1510), `deselectAll` (NetworkEditorModel.swift:509-521), `toggleNodeInSelection` (NetworkEditorModel.swift:465-477), marquee (NetworkEditorModel.swift:1446-1473) and Tab-walking (NetworkEditorModel.swift:1876-1892). The adjacency the commands would need already exists: `linksAttached(to:)` at NetworkEditorModel.swift:2195-2207.
findings.proposed_fix: Add to `NetworkEditorModel`: `selectConnectedComponent()` (undirected BFS from the current selection over `links`), `selectDownstream()` / `selectUpstream()` (directed BFS following `fromNodeID`/`toNodeID`), `invertSelection()` and `selectAll(kind:)`. All build on `linksAttached(to:)` and commit through the existing `setNodeSelection(_:)` so normalisation, nudge-run termination and the status bar stay consistent. Surface them in Edit, below Select All / Deselect All (QnetCommands.swift:430-450), and in the canvas empty-area context menu next to Select All (NetworkCanvasView.swift:799-802). Route each through `NSApp.sendAction` first, as Select All already does, so a focused text field is not hijacked.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Select one station in a branched network and choose Edit ▸ Select Connected: every node in that weakly-connected component is selected and the status bar count matches. Select Downstream from a mid-chain buffer selects only what is reachable following link direction. Invert Selection on a 10-node network with 3 selected leaves 7 selected. Each command is disabled when it would be a no-op. None of them registers an undo entry (selection is UI state, per the comment at NetworkEditorModel.swift:2243-2245).
findings.risk: Low. The traversals must terminate on cycles — this is a feedback-network tool, so a visited set is mandatory, and self-loops (see finding #2) must not spin. `setNodeSelection` calls `endNudgeRun()` on a selection change (NetworkEditorModel.swift:481), which is the desired behaviour here.

findings.title: Add a canvas overview navigator and fit-width / fit-height
findings.user_impact: Beyond about thirty nodes there is no way to see where you are. The only orientation aids are the two legacy scrollers and the pan-offset readout; there is no thumbnail navigator of the kind Visio, yEd and Simulink all provide, and no Fit Width / Fit Height. The zoom preset menu offers only 50 %, 100 % and 200 %, so there is no quick way to reach 25 % on a wide tandem chain other than repeated ⌘−.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasOverlays.swift:97-100 — the preset list is the literal `[0.5, 1.0, 2.0]`. Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:1566-1586 offers only `zoomToFit` and `zoomToFitSelection`; there is no width- or height-only fit and `CanvasTransform.fitting` takes a single margin. Navigation aids present: scrollers (NetworkCanvasScrollContainer.swift:39-88), pan readout (ContentView.swift:905-917), `findAndRevealNode` (NetworkEditorModel.swift:1487-1501), Tab-walk reveal (NetworkCanvasScrollContainer.swift:664-694). Nothing renders a scaled overview.
findings.proposed_fix: Two parts, either independently useful. (a) Cheap: extend the zoom preset menu to 25/50/75/100/150/200/400 % and add Fit Width / Fit Height built on a variant of `fit(nodes:)` that constrains one axis only — a few lines against the existing `CanvasTransform.fitting`. (b) A navigator: a collapsible floating panel in the canvas's bottom-left (where `CanvasClassLegend` already sits, NetworkCanvasView.swift:65-69) drawing the world bbox with one dot per node and a draggable viewport rectangle. It can be built from `CanvasScene.bounds(of:)` plus the same `CanvasScrollMetrics` maths that already computes on-screen overflow, and must reuse `canvasFloatingPanel()` (NetworkCanvasOverlays.swift:11-36) so its chrome matches the zoom cluster.
findings.acceptance_criteria: The zoom menu offers at least 25 % through 400 % plus Fit Width and Fit Height, and each lands at the stated scale. If the navigator ships: it shows every node, its viewport rectangle tracks pan and zoom live, dragging the rectangle pans the canvas, it hides when the network fits entirely on screen, and it costs no measurable per-frame time in validation/canvas_perf/run_canvas_bench.sh during a node drag.
findings.risk: A navigator that redraws on every `nodes` publish would add a full layer to the drag frame budget documented in CanvasGeometry.swift's CanvasProfiler comment. Throttle it the way the scroller coordinator already throttles its three publishers to 16 ms (NetworkCanvasScrollContainer.swift:158-168), or freeze it during `isDraggingNode` as the route plan is frozen.

findings.title: Persist Snap to Grid instead of resetting it per tab and per launch
findings.user_impact: Snap to Grid is off by default, lives on the editor rather than in preferences, and is not written to the document or the tab-restore record. A user who turns it on, opens a second tab, and starts drawing gets un-snapped placement again; quitting and relaunching loses it entirely. In MATLAB, Visio and OmniGraffle this is a sticky application preference.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:86-89 — `@Published var snapToGrid: Bool = false`, per-editor (i.e. per tab). Sources/Qnet/TabPersistence.swift:82-83 persists only `canvasScale` and `canvasPanOffset`. Sources/Qnet/Models.swift:922-923 — `NetworkDocument` carries `canvasScale`/`canvasPanOffset` and no snap flag. Nothing in Sources/Qnet/AppSettings.swift references it (grep for snapToGrid across Sources/Qnet lists only ContentView, DesignSystem symbol, DSGallery).
findings.proposed_fix: Move the default into `AppSettings` as an `@AppStorage`-backed preference ("canvas.snapToGrid"), have each new `NetworkEditorModel` seed `snapToGrid` from it, and write back when the View menu item / zoom-cluster toggle / context-menu toggle flips it — those three already share one binding path (ContentView.swift:254-257, NetworkCanvasOverlays.swift:142-152, NetworkCanvasView.swift:810-813). Leave the per-tab `@Published` in place so an individual tab can still differ within a session. Consider defaulting it ON for new documents: the grid is drawn (NetworkCanvasLayers.swift:25-52) and `SmartGuides` already arbitrates against it per axis, so snapping on is the more guiding default for the from-scratch workflow the user asked for.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Turn Snap to Grid on, press ⌘N: the new tab opens with it on and the status-bar snap glyph is accented. Quit and relaunch: still on. Turning it off in one tab does not silently change another tab that is already open. `validation/design_lint.sh` passes.
findings.risk: Low. If the default flips to ON, existing documents whose nodes sit off-grid will pull to the grid on their first drag — that is exactly what the per-axis grid-vs-guide arbitration at NetworkCanvasView.swift:579-592 was written to handle gracefully, and ⌃ still overrides, but it is a visible behaviour change worth a changelog line.

findings.title: Write a "Building a Network" help topic and surface the gesture vocabulary on the canvas
findings.user_impact: The canvas has a rich, well-designed gesture vocabulary — ⌥-drag duplicates, ⌃-drag suspends snapping, ⇧/⌘-click extends, Space or middle-button pans, ⌥Tab walks links, double-click opens the inspector — and essentially none of it is discoverable. It is documented in source comments and in tooltips the user must already be hovering the right control to see. Help ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts lists the keys (correctly, and generated from the live menu bar) but there is no page that teaches the workflow: place nodes, connect them, set parameters, run.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/QnetHelpWindow.swift:37-42 — the Workflows group is keyboardShortcuts, inspector, solverInputs, testSets, general, interactiveShell; there is no canvas topic. Sources/Qnet/AlgorithmHelp.swift:813-864 (`general`) covers only tab-restore and blocking-mode preferences. The gesture list exists but only as `KeyboardShortcutReference.unprintedKeys` (Sources/Qnet/KeyboardShortcutReference.swift:139-151), rendered as a bare table at the bottom of the shortcuts page. Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasOverlays.swift:161-170 is the only on-canvas guidance and it names exactly one key.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a `HelpTopic.buildingNetworks` in the Workflows group with an `AlgorithmHelp` blob in the same ASCII shape as the others (title, underlined headings, four-space-indented tables so `HelpMarkup` typesets it identically), walking the from-scratch path end to end: place with S/B/O/X, connect with L (and drag-to-connect once finding #3 lands), edit with ⌘I or double-click, arrange with the guides and Arrange menu, then Analyze and Run. Cite every key through `KeyboardShortcutReference.key(for:)` rather than spelling glyphs, which design_lint enforces for ⌘-digit anyway. Then extend the empty-canvas state (see finding #8) with a link into that topic, and add a per-tool hint line to the canvas status bar's tool segment (ContentView.swift:845-852) that says what the active tool's next click will do — the Link tool already prints such a line to the status *log* (NetworkEditorModel.swift:1977), which is the wrong place for transient guidance.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Help ▸ Building a Network exists in the Workflows group, is reachable by ⌘F search within the Help window, renders through the same `HelpMarkup` path as the other topics, and `Qnet --dump-help buildingNetworks` prints it headlessly. Its key references match the live menu bar (no `KeyboardShortcutReference.auditTable` drift). design_lint.sh passes, including the ▸ menu-path rule and the no-bare-⌘-digit rule.
findings.risk: Low. `HelpTopic` raw values are persisted in `@AppStorage("help.lastTopic")` (QnetHelpWindow.swift:26-27), so add a new case rather than renaming any existing one. Every topic needs its help-anchor string (QnetHelpWindow.swift:204 pattern) and its `AlgorithmHelp` mapping (QnetHelpWindow.swift:248) or the window will crash or blank.

findings.title: Let arrow keys scroll the canvas when nothing is selected, and Escape cancel an in-flight drag
findings.user_impact: Two small gestures every scrolling/dragging surface has. (1) With nothing selected, pressing an arrow key does absolutely nothing — the canvas swallows the event and `nudgeSelection` returns early, so the view will not scroll and the keystroke does not fall through to the responder chain either. (2) There is no way to abort a node drag in progress: pressing Escape mid-drag deselects but leaves the nodes wherever the pointer has dragged them, and the only recovery is ⌘Z after release.
findings.evidence: (1) Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasScrollContainer.swift:628-631 routes all four arrow key codes to `editor.nudgeSelection(...)` unconditionally and never calls `super.keyDown`; Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:1803-1806 `guard !ids.isEmpty else { return }`. (2) Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasScrollContainer.swift:606-610 maps Escape to `editor.deselectAll()`, which (NetworkEditorModel.swift:509-521) clears selection state but does not touch `dragStartPositions`, `dragNodeID` or the open `beginMutation` group in `CanvasContentView` (NetworkCanvasView.swift:168-176, 493).
findings.proposed_fix: (1) In the arrow branch, when `editor.selectionUnion.isEmpty` and `selectedLinkID == nil`, call `editor.pan(by:)` by one grid cell (four with ⇧) instead of nudging — same key, unambiguous meaning, and it matches the way the scrollers' line-step already works (NetworkCanvasScrollContainer.swift:228-229). (2) Give the editor a `cancelDrag()` that restores `dragStartPositions`, closes the mutation without registering (or registers-then-undoes), clears the guides and resets `isDraggingNode`; have Escape call it when a drag is in flight, before falling through to `deselectAll()`. The canvas holds the drag state in `@State`, so expose the cancel as a flag the canvas observes (mirroring how `snapSuspended` is published back, NetworkCanvasView.swift:560-561) rather than moving the drag state into the model.
findings.acceptance_criteria: With nothing selected, pressing ↓ scrolls the canvas down one grid cell and the pan segment in the status bar updates; with a node selected, ↓ still nudges the node as before. Start dragging a group, press Escape before releasing: the nodes snap back to where they started, the alignment guides vanish, and the Edit menu shows no new "Undo Move Nodes" entry.
findings.risk: Escape currently has exactly one meaning on the canvas — Deselect All — and the comment at NetworkCanvasScrollContainer.swift:606-609 stresses that it is the single implementation shared with ⌥⌘A and the context menu. Cancel-drag must be strictly conditional on a drag being in flight so that contract is preserved when nothing is dragging.

findings.title: Make the Multi-Select tool's silent self-demotion to Pointer explicit, or drop the tool
findings.user_impact: Completing a marquee with the Multi-Select tool silently switches the active tool to Pointer, so the palette selection and the status bar's tool segment change under the user without them doing anything. This directly contradicts the canvas's stated contract that only H, the palette and Space change the tool, and it makes M a one-shot mode that cannot be used twice in a row. Since Pointer already gives a marquee on any empty-canvas drag past 5 pt, the Multi-Select tool is largely redundant.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:1474 — the last line of `finalizeMultiSelect` is `selectedTool = .select`; the same happens in `selectAll()` at NetworkEditorModel.swift:1508. The contract it breaks is stated at Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasView.swift:39-40 ("A click never changes the active tool; H, the palette and the Space bar are the only ways to reach the Pan tool") and reinforced at NetworkCanvasView.swift:746-747 and :768-770. Pointer's own marquee is at NetworkCanvasView.swift:686-699 (threshold 5 pt, NetworkCanvasView.swift:198).
findings.proposed_fix: Pick one and be explicit. Either (a) keep Multi-Select sticky — delete the `selectedTool = .select` assignments at NetworkEditorModel.swift:1474 and :1508 so the tool the user chose stays chosen, and let Pointer's own marquee cover the casual case; or (b) retire the tool, folding its only distinct behaviour (marquee starts on press with no threshold) into Pointer, and remove `.multiSelect` from `EditorTool` (Models.swift:39), the palette groups, the Tools menu and the M hotkey. (a) is the smaller change and preserves the M badge users may already have learned. Whichever is chosen, the doc comment at NetworkCanvasView.swift:39-40 must be corrected — today it asserts a rule the code breaks.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Under (a): pick M, drag a marquee, release — the palette still shows Multi-Select selected and the status bar still reads "Multi-Select", and a second marquee can be drawn immediately without re-picking the tool. Under (b): `EditorTool.allCases` no longer contains `.multiSelect`, M is free, `EditorTool(shortcutCharacter:)` and `KeyboardShortcutReference`'s conventions block (KeyboardShortcutReference.swift:216-218, which names "V M H · S B O X · L") are updated together, and `QNET_MENU_AUDIT=1` reports no orphaned key. design_lint.sh and swift build pass either way.
findings.risk: Option (b) touches `EditorTool`, which is the single source of truth for the palette, the Tools menu, `ToolShortcutGuard` and the status bar; a partial removal would leave a menu item bound to a case that no longer exists. Option (a) is nearly risk-free but changes what happens after ⌘A (Select All currently also forces Pointer), so verify Select All still leaves a usable tool state.

dimension: Building a network from scratch — archetypes, drag & drop, guidance

already_good.what: Live per-station stability feedback while typing. The inspector shows λ, c·μ and ρ with a tinted value and an inline warning at ρ ≥ 1 ("S1 is unstable, the queue grows without bound") and at ρ ≥ 0.95, in both the docked pane and the modal sheet, recomputed from a draft copy before Save. This is the single best guidance feature in the app and must not be touched.

The docked Inspector pane is visible by default, follows the canvas selection, commits on blur/Return, coalesces consecutive commits into one undo step, never writes an invalid draft, and logs a named warning when an invalid edit is discarded. Parameter entry is therefore already only 2 clicks per node once the node exists.

The FlagBar already exposes Analytical / Re-entrant / Warnings as pills with rich popovers, including per-criterion diffusion-friendliness checklists and the verbatim warning list. The presentation layer for pre-run guidance exists and is good; only its data supply is broken (see findings).

MethodAdvisor already answers "is this network in the method's domain?" per method, with suitability ranking (Recommended/Applicable/Caution/Experimental/Unavailable), assumptions, cost and outputs, and it actually runs ProductFormExporter as an applicability preview rather than guessing.

The Link tool chains: after a link is made, the target becomes the new start, so an 8-node chain costs 8 clicks rather than 14. Class candidacy is derived from incoming links and duplicate (from,to,class) links are refused with an explanatory status line.

Undo is snapshot-based and already captures the auto-naming counters alongside nodes/links/bufferMode, so any bulk insert wrapped in performMutation will undo cleanly, including node names. This is exactly the hook an archetype insert needs.

RandomNetworkGenerator is a complete, working precedent for programmatic network construction: it builds Src/B/S/Sink nodes, per-class routing matrices, and back-solves external arrival rates to hit a target ρ at every station, with a deterministic seed and a legible left-to-right layout. An archetype builder should reuse its Result type and layout constants rather than invent new ones.

PicturePickerSheet is a finished, DS-compliant gallery sheet — DSSheet chrome, sectioned LazyVGrid, arrow-key navigation, double-click to choose, Return/Esc — and is the right shape to clone for an archetype gallery.

Direct manipulation on the canvas is mature: ⌥-drag duplicates, ⌃ suspends snap and guides for one drag, smart alignment guides, snap-to-grid, marquee select, align/distribute, arrow-key nudge runs coalesced into one undo step, and double-clicking a node opens its parameter sheet.

Distribution parameters carry real metadata — units ("1/time", "time"), min/max with exclusivity, per-parameter help, closed-form mean and SCV formulas, and a station-only filter that hides the Poisson count law from service pickers.

The 50 bundled .bnet examples are curated and machine-checked: example_contracts.py asserts the tandem family's exact topology (1 source, d buffers, d stations, 1 sink, 2d+1 links), unique ids, ρ = 0.9 and exact E[N] = 9 per station. This is a ready-made specification for what a generated "tandem" archetype must produce.
already_good.evidence: validation/example_contracts.py:31-100, 118-152; input/examples/3dtandem.inf.bnet (source lambda=1.0, station rate=1.1111111 → ρ=0.9)

already_good.what: The empty canvas is not blank: an overlay teaches the first two moves and names the ⇧⌘O example shortcut, and it is an overlay rather than a replacement so the canvas keeps its frame and gestures.
Edit ▸ Find Node… (⌘F) live-filters node names, previews the first six matches with kind glyphs, and reveals/zooms the first match — real navigation for a large network.

findings.title: Add a network archetype library with a gallery sheet and an undo-safe bulk insert
findings.user_impact: There is no template library of any kind. The only ways to get a network are: click-place every node by hand, roll dice with Generate Random Network, or hunt for a file through an NSOpenPanel. A user who wants "a 3-station tandem line at ρ = 0.9" — the canonical object this application analyses — must place 8 nodes, draw 7 links, switch the buffer regime, and type 4 rates. Counted from the code: 12 clicks to place the 8 nodes (4 palette clicks + 8 canvas clicks), 1 palette click + 8 canvas clicks for the chain, 2 clicks for Network ▸ Buffer Model ▸ Infinite, 1 click back to the Pointer, then 8 clicks to select and focus the 4 rate fields = 32 clicks plus 4 typed numbers. With the single-letter hotkeys it is still 27 clicks. MATLAB/Maple ship a template gallery; Qnet ships none, and the words archetype, template and preset appear nowhere in the source outside the DS token vocabulary.
findings.evidence: grep for archetype|template|preset|starter across Sources/Qnet returns only DS token comments and AIPaneView starter prompts; Sources/Qnet/QnetCommands.swift:206-231 (File menu: New/Open/Open Recent/Open Example only), 688-731 (Network menu: Buffer Model, Network Model, Analyze, Primitives, Straighten, Generate Random Network — no insert/template); Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:402-427 (handleCanvasTap: one node per click), 2083-2113 (addNode)
findings.acceptance_criteria: From a launched app with an empty canvas: File ▸ New from Template… → Tandem Line → set Stations 3, ρ 0.9 → Insert produces, in ≤ 4 clicks total, a network of 1 source, 3 buffers, 3 stations, 1 sink and 7 links with infiniteBuffers = true; Run ▸ Run Whitt QNA succeeds with no export error; the FlagBar Analytical pill lights (exact Jackson); every station reports ρ = 0.900 in the Inspector; one ⌘Z restores the empty canvas and the Edit menu reads "Undo Insert Tandem Line"; a second insert into the same canvas produces S4/S5/S6 rather than a second S1. validation/design_lint.sh and validation/gui_runtime_contracts.sh both pass and swift build is green.
findings.risk: design_lint.sh will reject literal SF Symbol strings, frame/radius/stroke literals, .foregroundStyle(.secondary) and any hand-built animation in the two new views — compose DS.Symbol.*, DS.Layout.*, DS.Color.text* and DS.Motion.* only, and read accessibility through @DSAccessibility. DSEmptyState titles added anywhere must be Title Case noun phrases (design_lint.sh checks the literal). Assigning nodes/links directly instead of going through insertSubnetwork would reproduce the counter bug reported separately. gui_runtime_contracts.sh greps QnetGUIApp.swift for exact runner strings and counts — adding a sheet and a menu action touches none of them, but re-verify after editing that file.

findings.title: Ship the 50 example networks inside Qnet.app and stop resolving them from the working directory

findings.title: Stop discarding the exporter's diagnosis while a network is being built — the flag bar reports "no problems" for every incomplete network
findings.user_impact: During the entire construction of a network the app knows exactly what is wrong and throws it away. SRBMExporter.computeData returns precise, user-facing reasons — "The network has no sink node.", "Station S1 has no buffer feeding into it.", "The source must connect (possibly via a buffer) to station S1." — but on failure the silent analysis sets networkHasWarnings = false and networkWarningList = [], so the Warnings popover affirmatively tells the user "The latest analysis found no problems: every station is stable (ρ < 1) and the routing structure is consistent." The station ρ badges silently vanish for the same reason. The real message only appears as a modal "SRBM Export Failed" alert after the user presses Run. Worse: the mandatory Buffer-before-Station pairing is documented nowhere in the UI — not in the empty state, not in the Station tool tooltip — so the natural build (Src → S1 → S2 → S3 → Sink) is silently invalid, cheerfully reported as having no problems, and fails only at Run.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:6303-6312 (failure branch clears networkHasWarnings and networkWarningList, and in quiet mode logs nothing); Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:1664-1666 (refreshStationUtilisation drops the failure reason); Sources/Qnet/FlagBarView.swift:379-383 ("The latest analysis found no problems…"); Sources/Qnet/NetworkExporter.swift:13-32 and Sources/Qnet/SRBMExporter.swift:76-118 (the diagnoses being discarded); Sources/Qnet/Models.swift:134-141 (Station/Buffer tooltips never mention the pairing rule)
findings.proposed_fix: Add a published `structuralProblems: [String]` to NetworkEditorModel beside networkWarningList (NetworkEditorModel.swift:176-183). In analyzeActiveTabIfNeeded's failure branch (QnetGUIApp.swift:6303) set structuralProblems = [err.localizedDescription] plus a computed checklist of what is still missing (no source / no sink / no station / stations without a buffer / nodes with no incoming or outgoing link / source not reaching S1) instead of clearing everything, and keep hasBeenAnalyzed = true. Give the FlagBar Warnings pill a third state — "Incomplete" (DS.Color.info fill, DS.Color.infoText ink) — whose popover lists the structural problems as a to-do checklist with the offending node names, reusing the exact ForEach/DSRule body already at FlagBarView.swift:388-406. Do the same in refreshStationUtilisation (NetworkEditorModel.swift:1664): keep the failure reason rather than only emptying the badge dictionary. Separately, extend the Station tool tooltip (Models.swift:134-135) to say a station must be fed by exactly one buffer, and say the same in the empty state.
findings.acceptance_criteria: On a canvas holding one source and one station with no sink, the Warnings pill reads "Incomplete" and its popover lists "The network has no sink node." Placing Src → S1 → Sink with no buffer makes the popover read "Station S1 has no buffer feeding into it." and name S1. Once B1 is inserted between Src and S1 the pill returns to "None" and the station's ρ badge reappears. No modal alert is the first place any of these sentences is seen.
findings.risk: FlagBarView is the documented exception to the .dsChromeBar lint rule (design_lint.sh header) — do not restructure its chrome while adding the state. DS.Color.info used as ink must be spelled DS.Color.infoText or the signal-colour-as-ink lint fires. The new pill state must not change the meaning of networkHasWarnings, which MethodAdvisor reads for its Caution ranking (MethodChooserView.swift:119).

findings.title: Structural edits never invalidate the analysis, so the flag bar goes stale for the whole build
findings.user_impact: Adding a node, adding a link, deleting a node and deleting a link all go through performMutation, which does not post .bnetNetworkParametersDidChange. Only the nine parameter mutations call noteParametersChanged(). The silent re-analysis is driven exclusively by that notification and by the guard `!editor.hasBeenAnalyzed`, so from the moment the analysis has run once, the whole structural build — every node and every link — leaves the Analytical, Re-entrant and Warnings pills showing results for a network that no longer exists. On a fresh tab the opposite failure occurs: the empty-canvas early return leaves hasBeenAnalyzed false, so the pills say "The network has not been analysed yet" until the user happens to edit a parameter, which is the only event that will ever fire the analysis.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:2083-2113 (addNode → performMutation, no noteParametersChanged), 2025-2044 (Add Link), 567-598 (deleteNode/deleteLink), 1049-1058 (noteParametersChanged is the only poster), 2300-2306 (performMutation posts nothing); Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:844-850 (the only quiet re-analysis trigger), 6261 (guard !hasBeenAnalyzed), 6262-6271 (empty-canvas early return leaves hasBeenAnalyzed false)
findings.proposed_fix: Post the invalidation from the structural mutations too. The cleanest single point is performMutation itself (NetworkEditorModel.swift:2300-2306) and endMutation (2319-2340): after the block runs, if nodes/links/infiniteBuffers changed relative to the snapshot, set hasBeenAnalyzed = false and post .bnetNetworkParametersDidChange — endMutation already computes exactly that comparison at 2334-2337, so the test is free there. This also removes the need for individual call sites to remember. Debounce on the receiving side rather than the sending side: the app's onReceive at QnetGUIApp.swift:844-850 should coalesce bursts (a chain of link clicks) the same way $nodes.combineLatest(...).debounce(150ms) already protects refreshStationUtilisation (NetworkEditorModel.swift:21-26). Also drop the empty-canvas early return's asymmetry (QnetGUIApp.swift:6262-6271) so hasBeenAnalyzed is set in both quiet and loud paths.
findings.acceptance_criteria: On a valid network, deleting the sink makes the Warnings pill change within ~200 ms without any parameter edit. Adding a feedback link A→B→A lights the Re-entrant pill immediately. Building a fresh tandem from an empty canvas lights the Analytical pill as soon as the last link is drawn, with no intervening parameter edit. Dragging a node (which changes only positions) does not re-run the analysis.
findings.risk: performMutation is called from drag paths and from every parameter mutation, so an un-debounced notification would re-run SRBMExporter.computeData per frame; the debounce on the receive side is mandatory. restore() already posts the notification (NetworkEditorModel.swift:2292), so undo must not post twice — gate the new post on the same before/after comparison endMutation uses.

findings.title: Every hand-built network is born exactly unstable: default source and default station both carry rate = 1.0, giving ρ = 1.000
findings.user_impact: A node placed by clicking gets NetworkNode's default init: exponential, "rate=1.0", one server. A source therefore offers λ = 1.0 and a station serves at c·μ = 1.0, so the first network anyone builds by hand has ρ = 1.000 at every station — the exact boundary of instability. AnalyticalTractability short-circuits to unstable() and reports nothing; networkWarnings emits "station 1 is overloaded (ρ = 1.0000 ≥ 1)"; the Inspector paints ρ in danger ink. The user's first experience of a self-built network is an unstable one, for no reason: the bundled examples all use λ = 1.0 with μ = 1.1111111 (ρ = 0.9), and RandomNetworkGenerator defaults to targetRho 0.9 precisely because that is the useful regime.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/Models.swift:876-880 (bufferSize 1, numberOfServers 1, distribution .exponential, distributionParameters exponential.defaultParameters), 205-208 (exponential defaultParameters = "rate=1.0"); Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:2106 (addNode constructs NetworkNode with all defaults); Sources/Qnet/AnalyticalTractability.swift:64-68, 579-588 (ρ ≥ 1 → unstable()); Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:6667-6672 (overload warning); input/examples/3dtandem.inf.bnet (source lambda=1.0, station rate=1.1111111); Sources/Qnet/RandomNetworkGenerator.swift:45 (targetRho = 0.9)
findings.proposed_fix: Give the click-to-place path a station default that is stable against the default source rather than exactly critical. In addNode (NetworkEditorModel.swift:2083-2113), construct a station with distributionParameters "rate=1.1111111" (μ = λ/0.9, matching every bundled example and the ρ = 0.9 the validation contract asserts) while leaving NetworkNode's own init defaults alone so no saved document changes meaning. Sources keep λ = 1.0 and should also arrive as .poisson with "lambda=1.0" rather than .exponential, since that is what every bundled example uses, what QueueDistribution.pickerName is worded for, and what MethodAdvisor's sourcesArePoisson test looks for. State the resulting ρ in the status line addNode already emits ("Added station S1 — ρ = 0.900 against the default source rate") so the number is taught rather than merely defaulted.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Placing Src1 → B1 → S1 → Sink1 with no parameter edits yields ρ = 0.900 in the Inspector, no overload warning, and the Analytical pill lit as exact Jackson. Opening any bundled example still shows its own saved rates unchanged. --dump-rho on a freshly placed chain reports 0.9.
findings.risk: AnalyticalTractability's Jackson branch requires Poisson or exponential arrivals (AnalyticalTractability.swift:194), so switching the source default to .poisson keeps it eligible; verify it does not disturb MethodAdvisor.hasClassIndependentService (MethodChooserView.swift:500-526), which reads the "rate" key for stations only. Changing NetworkNode.init's defaults instead of addNode's call site would alter how old documents decode — do not.

findings.title: Generate Random Network bypasses loadNetwork, so the name counters stay at zero and the next placed station is a duplicate "S1"
findings.user_impact: createRandomNetworkTab assigns editor.nodes / editor.links / editor.infiniteBuffers directly instead of calling loadNetwork(document:). loadNetwork is the only place that re-primes stationCount/bufferCount/sourceCount/sinkCount from the loaded names. So immediately after generating a 4-station random network, pressing S and clicking creates a second node named "S1". Since every exporter orders stations by the numeric suffix of the name (NodeNaming), two stations called S1 make stationOrderIsAmbiguous true, which silently degrades every result label to positional "S1 … Sn" — and the export order between the two S1s is decided by whatever the sort happens to produce. The generated tab is also never marked clean, so it shows an unsaved-changes dot with no user edit, and its parameter cache is never wiped from the previous document.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:1169-1172 (direct assignment, no loadNetwork, no markDocumentClean); Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:1417-1421 (counters re-primed only in loadNetwork), 2089-2103 (addNode names purely from the counters), 719-722 (paste re-primes but add does not), 327-342 (stationOrderIsAmbiguous / stationName(atExportIndex:) fall back to positional names)
findings.proposed_fix: Two changes. (a) Make createRandomNetworkTab go through the same door as every other document load: build a NetworkDocument from the generator Result and call newTab.editor.loadNetwork(document:) (QnetGUIApp.swift:1169-1172), which primes the counters, clears the parameter cache and marks the document clean. (b) Belt and braces: make addNode re-prime the counters with the same max(counter, maxNameIndex(...)) lines pasteClipboardContents already runs (NetworkEditorModel.swift:719-722) before it increments, so no future direct-assignment path can reintroduce duplicate names. The proposed insertSubnetwork must do the same.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Network ▸ Generate Random Network… with 4 stations, then press S and click: the new station is named S5, not S1. The generated tab shows no unsaved-changes dot until the user edits it. editor.stationOrderIsAmbiguous is false throughout.
findings.risk: loadNetwork resets canvasScale and canvasPanOffset from the document (NetworkEditorModel.swift:1384-1385), so build the NetworkDocument with the scale the random tab is meant to open at. loadNetwork also emits its own "Loaded network with N nodes" status line — either suppress it or let it precede the existing "Generated Random N" line. loadNetwork calls markDocumentClean, which is desired here but changes the tab-close guard's answer for a generated-but-unedited tab (TabClosing.swift:126).

findings.title: Edit ▸ Clear Canvas… promises an undo it does not provide
findings.user_impact: The destructive confirmation says, verbatim, "Every node and link in “X” will be removed. This can be undone with Edit ▸ Undo." NetworkEditorModel.clear() performs the deletion outside performMutation and registers nothing with the undo manager — it wipes nodes, links, the parameter cache, the four name counters and every analysis field, then calls markDocumentClean(). A user experimenting with a from-scratch build who clears and then reaches for ⌘Z loses the whole network, and the app told them they would not.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:1101-1110 (ConfirmAlert text at 1106, then editor.clear()); Sources/Qnet/NetworkEditorModel.swift:1331-1371 (clear() — no performMutation, no registerReversal, and markDocumentClean at 1370)
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the document-mutating part of clear() in performMutation("Clear Canvas") (NetworkEditorModel.swift:2300). The existing NetworkSnapshot already carries nodes, links, infiniteBuffers and all four name counters (2246-2254), so a single wrap restores the network and its naming state exactly. Keep the non-document resets (selection, hover, tractability fields, hasBeenAnalyzed) outside the block, and move or drop markDocumentClean() so a cleared-then-undone document is not reported as clean. If clear() is deliberately meant to be non-undoable, change the alert text instead; do not leave the two disagreeing.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Build any network, Edit ▸ Clear Canvas… → Clear, then ⌘Z: every node, link, buffer regime and node name returns, the Edit menu reads "Undo Clear Canvas", and adding a new station afterwards continues the numbering rather than restarting at S1.

dimension: Window and pane layout, crowding, and MATLAB-style pop-out panels

already_good.what: A single, well-factored auxiliary-window factory already exists and is the exact template a pop-out mechanism should generalize. `AuxiliaryWindow.make(id:title:contentSize:minSize:resizable:transparentTitlebar:root:)` builds an `NSHostingController`-backed `NSWindow`, stamps a `qnet.aux.` identifier so ⌘W can tell it from the canvas window, sets `tabbingMode = .disallowed`, `isReleasedWhenClosed = false`, lists it in the Window menu, and wires Escape-to-close through a weak `WindowRef`.
