findings.title: Add a generic detach/re-attach mechanism for the six side panes
findings.user_impact: There is no pop-out of any kind. A user with a 27" display and a laptop screen cannot put the Shell on one and the canvas on the other; a user who wants a large Results table must instead shrink the canvas inside one window. MATLAB, Maple, Xcode and RStudio all undock. Qnet's only multi-window surfaces are six read-only reference panels (About, Help, Release Notes, Method Chooser, Network Model, DS Gallery); none of the six working panes (Tools, Inspector, Status, Results, Shell, AI) can leave the main window.
findings.evidence: Absence verified: `grep -rni 'detach|undock|pop ?out|tear.?off|NSPanel' Sources/Qnet/*.swift` returns only unrelated `Task.detached` hits (QnetGUIApp.swift:718, 735; StartupDependencyChecker.swift:399) and a prose use at ResultsWorkspace.swift:302. The whole layout is one fixed split tree at Sources/Qnet/ContentView.swift:94-208; the only NSWindow factory is Sources/Qnet/WindowSupport.swift:94-128 and its six callers.
findings.proposed_fix:
Use NSWindow via the existing `AuxiliaryWindow` factory, NOT a second SwiftUI scene: `tabs`/`activeTabID` are `@State` on the App struct (QnetGUIApp.swift:536-537), so a `WindowGroup`/`Window` scene cannot be handed them, and a new WindowGroup would resurrect the automatic-tabbing problem QnetGUIApp.swift:574-578 deliberately killed.

New file `Sources/Qnet/PaneDetachment.swift`:
(1) `enum DetachablePane: String, CaseIterable { case palette, inspector, status, results, shell, ai }` — 1:1 with `FocusRouter.Pane` (PaneChrome.swift:43-47) minus `.canvas`.
(2) `@MainActor final class PaneDetachmentModel: ObservableObject` with `@Published private(set) var detached: Set<DetachablePane>`, `detach/reattach/toggle`, persisted to UserDefaults key `panes.detached` as a comma-joined raw-value list, and a `windows: [DetachablePane: NSWindow]` table mirroring the `retained` statics the six aux windows use.
(3) `@MainActor final class ActiveTabBox: ObservableObject { @Published var editor: NetworkEditorModel?; @Published var tabID: UUID?; @Published var title: String }` — THE piece that makes a detached pane keep talking to the right model. Feed it from the existing `.onChange(of: activeTabID, initial: true)` block at QnetGUIApp.swift:874-877, which already calls `appSettings.trackActiveEditor(activeEditor)` and `bindAIConversation()`. Without this a detached pane snapshots one editor and goes stale on tab switch — precisely the bug `MethodChooserWindow.show` papers over by calling `retained?.close()` and rebuilding every time (MethodChooserView.swift:702-718).
(4) `DetachedPaneHost: View` observes `ActiveTabBox` and renders the pane with `.environmentObject(box.editor!)` plus the app-level `terminalModel` / `appSettings` / `aiModel`. The pane views need no change — they all read from `@EnvironmentObject` already (InspectorPaneView.swift:40-41, ContentView.swift:1114-1117, StatusLog.swift, AIPaneView.swift); `ResultsWorkspaceView(tabID:networkTitle:)` takes explicit parameters, fed from the box. `TerminalPaneView` is `private` at ContentView.swift:1113 and must become internal (or move to its own file) so the host can build one.
(5) Extend `AuxiliaryWindow.make` (WindowSupport.swift:94-128) additively with three parameters, leaving the six existing callers untouched: `escapeCloses: Bool = true` (a detached Inspector must let Escape revert the field per InspectorPaneView.swift:19-25, not close the window); `fullScreenAuxiliary: Bool = false` → `window.collectionBehavior.insert(.fullScreenAuxiliary)`; and `onClose: (() -> Void)? = nil`, observed via `NSWindow.willCloseNotification` exactly as SettingsComponents.swift:278-291 already does, so closing a detached window RE-ATTACHES the pane instead of losing it.
(6) ContentView gates each pane on `appSettings.<x>PaneVisible && !detachment.isDetached(.<x>)`, and the same predicate feeds `topPanes` / `rightPanes` / `bottomPanes` / `outerPanes` (ContentView.swift:49-85) so `SplitViewConfigurator`'s `panes:` arrays stay truthful and saved divider sizes keep restoring.
(7) Terminal specifics: `SwiftTermView.attachHost` re-parents the model's single cached `TerminalHostView` into whichever wrapper asks (TerminalConsoleView.swift:600-625), so a detached Shell window inherits the LIVE shell — scrollback, running solver and all — with no restart. The invariant this creates is that exactly one `SwiftTermView` may be mounted at a time; step (6)'s predicate guarantees it, and it deserves an explicit assertion because two mounted wrappers would steal the host back and forth on every layout pass.
(8) Restoration: read `panes.detached` in `QnetGUIApp.init` next to the existing migration block (QnetGUIApp.swift:580-589) and re-open the windows from `applicationDidFinishLaunching`, where `DSGalleryWindow.show()` already demonstrates the pattern (QnetGUIApp.swift:30-32). Give each window `setFrameAutosaveName("QnetDetached.<pane>")`, matching QnetHelpWindow.swift:966 et al., so size and position come back per pane.
(9) Affordances: a `DSIconButton` with a new `DS.Symbol.detach` in each pane header's existing `trailing:` slot (DSSectionHeader.swift:56-58) — AIPaneView.swift:658, ContentView.swift:1172, InspectorPaneView.swift:93, ResultsWorkspace.swift:949, StatusLog.swift:255 all have one; ToolPaletteView.swift:18 uses the no-trailing overload and needs switching. Plus a `Window ▸ Detach ▸ …` / `Re-attach All Panes` group beside the Focus commands (WorkspaceCommands.swift:192-257) and double-click-the-header as the MATLAB gesture.
(10) Design-lint compliance: window sizes must be new `DS.Layout.Window.detachedPane*` constants added inside DesignSystem.swift (design_lint.sh forbids frame literals and forbids `extension DS…` outside that file), and the glyphs must be new `DS.Symbol.detach` / `.reattach` (lint forbids literal SF Symbol strings).
(11) ⌘W comes free: detached windows carry the `qnet.aux.` prefix (WindowSupport.swift:88, 115), so `MainWindowRegistry.keyWindowIsMainContent()` returns false and `closeTabOrKeyWindow` (QnetGUIApp.swift:1086-1092) closes the detached window, which via (5) re-attaches the pane.
findings.acceptance_criteria: With all panes shown: clicking the detach button in the Shell header (a) removes the Shell from the bottom row, (b) opens a titled, resizable, movable window whose terminal shows the SAME scrollback and the SAME running shell (`terminal.isShellRunning` still true, no new prompt), (c) leaves the AI pane occupying the bottom row with its divider position intact. Switching document tabs updates a detached Inspector/Status/Results window to the new tab's data. Closing the detached window with ⌘W or the red button puts the pane back in the split at its previous size. Quitting and relaunching re-opens the same detached windows at the same frames. `validation/design_lint.sh` and `validation/gui_runtime_contracts.sh` pass; `swift build` passes.
findings.risk: Two SwiftTermView instances mounted at once would fight over `TerminalModel.hostView` and thrash the terminal — mitigated by the mutual-exclusion predicate in step (6) plus an assertion. FocusRouter's single-slot handler dictionaries can be nil'd by the wrong pane's onDisappear (see the separate FocusRouter finding) — fix that first. `SplitViewConfigurator` restore is keyed on `sv.arrangedSubviews.count == panes.count` (ContentView.swift:1418-1419, 1437-1439), so the pane arrays MUST include the detach predicate or divider restoration silently no-ops. No validation contract touches layout: `gui_runtime_contracts.sh` greps only solver-launch strings (validation/gui_runtime_contracts.sh:16-60).

findings.title: Reduce default vertical over-subscription: the canvas becomes a letterbox after the first solver run
findings.user_impact: On first launch six panes are visible (Tools, Canvas, Inspector, Status, Shell, AI). The first time any solver runs, the Results workspace force-shows itself and — because the flag is `@AppStorage` — stays on forever. Seven panes then compete in a window whose default height cannot hold their ideal heights, so every row is squeezed to near its minimum. The canvas, the thing the user draws on, ends up roughly 1000 × 330 pt inside a 1500 × 900 window: under 40% of the frame, in a shape wrong for a left-to-right queueing network. The Shell — which the user wants as the centrepiece — gets 160–216 pt of usable height, about 11–15 rows at the default 12-pt mono.
findings.evidence: Pane defaults all-true except Results: Sources/Qnet/AppSettings.swift:135-139, 150. Results force-shows on the first run and persists: Sources/Qnet/ContentView.swift:319-325 with `@AppStorage("results.paneVisible")` at AppSettings.swift:401. Ideal heights sum to 1016 pt (top 520 + results 248 + bottom 248) against ~848 pt of content at `.defaultSize(width: 1500, height: 900)` minus the unified titlebar+toolbar: ContentView.swift:161-162, 171-172, 203-204; tokens at DesignSystem.swift:1148-1151; defaultSize at QnetGUIApp.swift:984, `.windowToolbarStyle(.unified)` at QnetGUIApp.swift:985. Minimums sum to 704 pt (320+192+192), so only ~144 pt of slack is distributed. Canvas loses a further 32 pt of tab bar and 24 pt of status bar (DesignSystem.swift:931, 933; ContentView.swift:109-113). Shell height = bottom row minus a 32-pt header (DesignSystem.swift:922); default shell font 12.0 at AppSettings.swift:132.
findings.proposed_fix: Three changes, none of which removes a capability. (a) Stop the unconditional force-show at ContentView.swift:319-325: on the first run, show Results only if it fits — i.e. only when the bottom row is hidden, or convert the behaviour to a one-shot nudge (show once, remember `results.autoShown` in AppSettings.Defaults, never force again). (b) Make Results and the bottom row mutually preferred rather than simultaneous by default: add a `Workspace Presets ▸ Solve` preset (canvas + shell + status, results off) and set the shipped default pane set to Tools/Canvas/Inspector/Status/Shell — AI off — so a fresh install starts at five panes, not six-going-on-seven. `applyWorkspacePreset` already exists (WorkspaceCommands.swift:295-311). (c) Raise `DS.Layout.Window.mainMinHeight` handling by lowering the *ideal* competition instead: set `canvasRowIdealHeight` and `bottomRowIdealHeight` so top+results+bottom ideals sum at or below 848 (e.g. 520 / 200 / 248 = 968 is still over; 480/184/224 = 888 is close, or accept that Results defaults off). Whatever numbers are chosen, add a comment in DesignSystem.swift stating the invariant `canvasRowIdealHeight + bottomRowIdealHeight + bottomRowIdealHeight <= defaultSize.height - 52` so the next editor cannot silently break it.
findings.acceptance_criteria: On a fresh UserDefaults domain, launching at the default 1500×900 and running one solver leaves the canvas drawing area at least 420 pt tall and the Shell at least 220 pt tall, measured from the split view's arranged subview frames. The sum of `canvasRowIdealHeight + bottomRowIdealHeight` (+ results ideal when Results ships on) is documented in DesignSystem.swift as ≤ the default content height. No pane loses a toggle, a shortcut or a preset.
findings.risk: Changing shipped `AppSettings.Defaults` changes what an existing user sees only if they have never toggled that pane (@AppStorage falls back to the default). The registered-defaults table at AppSettings.swift:661-674 must be updated in lockstep or `isPaneAtDefault` / the Settings "differs from defaults" badges drift. Ideal-height token changes reflow saved divider positions on the next launch for users who never dragged a divider.

findings.title: Make the Shell expressible as the centrepiece: add pane maximize/solo and a Shell workspace preset
findings.user_impact: The user's stated goal is that the embedded shell be THE centrepiece. Today it is the opposite: it lives in the last row of the window, shares that row with the AI pane, has an ideal height of 248 pt against the canvas row's 520, has no toolbar action of its own beyond a visibility toggle, appears in no workspace preset that gives it prominence, and there is no way to make any pane fill the window temporarily. A user reading 300 lines of solver output scrolls a 14-row viewport.
findings.evidence: Bottom row ideal/min 248/192 vs canvas row 520/320: Sources/Qnet/DesignSystem.swift:1148-1151, applied at ContentView.swift:161-162 and 203-204. Shell shares the bottom HSplit with the AI pane: ContentView.swift:176-207. Presets contain no shell-forward arrangement — "Run and Diagnose" turns on results+shell+status, still a thirds split: WorkspaceCommands.swift:84-90. No pane maximize exists anywhere: `grep -rni 'maximize|zoomPane|expandPane|soloPane' Sources/Qnet/*.swift` matches only prose in AlgorithmHelp.swift:1872. The toolbar's only Shell entry is the visibility toggle at ContentView.swift:288-294.
findings.proposed_fix: (a) Add a solo/maximize control to `DSSectionHeader`'s trailing slot for every pane (new `DS.Symbol.paneMaximize` / `.paneRestore` in DesignSystem.swift), backed by one `@AppStorage("panes.soloed")` string on AppSettings holding a `FocusRouter.Pane` raw value or empty. In ContentView, when a pane is soloed, render only that pane in the outer VSplit; restoring returns to the saved split sizes, which `SplitViewConfigurator.restore()` already reinstates from `SplitPane.*` keys (ContentView.swift:1435-1483) — no new persistence needed. Bind it to ⌃⌘⏎ (verify against `MenuShortcutAudit`, WindowSupport.swift:298-408, which asserts on collisions in DEBUG). (b) Add a `Workspace Presets ▸ Solve` entry — canvas + shell + status, everything else off — beside the four at WorkspaceCommands.swift:69-99, and surface the preset menu in the toolbar as a single `ToolbarItem` menu rather than only at menu depth 3. (c) Give the Shell a first-class place in the toolbar: a Run split-button (see the toolbar finding) whose secondary action is Focus Shell. (d) Once the detach mechanism lands, "detach the Shell to a second display" is the fullest expression of centrepiece and should be named in the Shell header's tooltip.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Clicking maximize in the Shell header makes the Shell fill the window's content area; clicking restore returns every divider to the exact position it held before (compare `SplitPane.*` UserDefaults values before and after). `Workspace Presets ▸ Solve` leaves canvas + shell + status visible and everything else hidden. A soloed pane survives a tab switch and is remembered across relaunch. Menu audit reports no shortcut collision (`QNET_MENU_AUDIT=1` exits 0).
findings.risk: Soloing must not unmount the Shell's `SwiftTermView` in a way that re-runs `attachHost` against a destroyed wrapper — keep the same conditional-presence discipline the tree already documents at ContentView.swift:88-93. If solo is implemented by removing panes from the split, `SplitViewConfigurator`'s `panes:` arrays must reflect the soloed set or its `arrangedSubviews.count == panes.count` guards silently disable save/restore.

findings.title: Fix the corner resize grip: it is misplaced and incomplete whenever the Results pane is visible
findings.user_impact: With the Results workspace showing (which happens automatically after the first solver run and then persists), the Shell/AI corner grip is drawn on the divider between the Canvas row and the Results row — nowhere near the Shell/AI divider it actually moves. Dragging it jumps two unrelated dividers. There is also no grip at the Results/Bottom divider or at the Results workspace's own internal split, so two of the four T-junctions in the full layout have no grip at all.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/CornerResizeOverlay.swift:91 computes `dividerY = outer.arrangedSubviews[0].frame.height` — the top row's height, i.e. the top|results boundary once Results is present. CornerResizeOverlay.swift:112-122 then places the `bottom.terminal.ai` grip at that same `dividerY`, although with Results visible the bottom row starts at top.height + divider + results.height. CornerResizeOverlay.swift:202 and 214-216 unconditionally drive `ofDividerAt: 0` of the outer split. The outer split's arranged subviews are [top, results, bottom] per ContentView.swift:49-54 and 94-208, so divider 0 is top|results and divider 1 is results|bottom.
findings.proposed_fix: Give `CornerSpot` an explicit `outerDividerIndex: Int` and compute each junction's y from the accumulated heights of the outer split's arranged subviews rather than always `arrangedSubviews[0].frame.height`. Derive the pane order from the same list `ContentView.outerPanes` builds (ContentView.swift:49-55) — pass it into `CornerResizeOverlay` alongside `aiPaneVisible`, or read `SplitViewConfigurator.Coordinator.panesByKey["OuterVSplit"]` (ContentView.swift:1348) which already holds it. Then: the two TopHSplit grips anchor to outer divider index 0; the terminal|ai grip anchors to the divider immediately above the bottom row (index 0 without Results, index 1 with it); and add a grip for the Results workspace's internal HSplit (ResultsWorkspace.swift:963-969) once that split is registered — it currently has no `SplitViewConfigurator`, so register it under `"ResultsHSplit"` first. `currentOuterY` and `moveDividers` take the index from the spot.
findings.acceptance_criteria: With Tools, Canvas, Inspector, Status, Results, Shell and AI all visible, each visible T-junction shows a grip centred on the actual divider crossing within 1 pt, and dragging each grip moves exactly the two dividers that meet there. With Results hidden, behaviour is unchanged from today. Verified by reading the arranged-subview frames at runtime, or by a screenshot comparison.
findings.risk: The overlay's coordinate space is the outer VSplit's frame (ContentView.swift:212-216); adding grips must not put a hit region over the Results filter row's text field. Registering the Results inner split adds a fourth key to `SplitRegistry`; the coupled-width mirror keys are an explicit set (`ContentView.swift:1354`) so it will not be mirrored by accident.

findings.title: Make the run-parameter and generator dialogs movable windows instead of pinned sheets
findings.user_impact: The user explicitly asked for movable popups. Ten dialogs in the app are SwiftUI sheets: they are glued to the top centre of the main window, cannot be dragged, and cover the canvas and the Shell while open. Setting up a Monte Carlo run means typing replication counts into a sheet that hides the very network those numbers describe, and hides the Shell where the previous run's output sits. MATLAB and Maple use movable modeless dialogs for exactly this.
findings.evidence: Ten `.sheet(` presentations: Sources/Qnet/ContentView.swift:303, 309, 315; NodeInspectorSections.swift:137; QnetGUIApp.swift:701, 710, 728, 745, 759, 763. The run-parameter sheet is the most-used path and is explicitly documented as such at RunParameterSheet.swift:6-9. Sheet geometry is already standardized and resizable-by-content via `DSSheetSize` (DSSheet.swift:24-112). The Settings window itself is a normal SwiftUI `Settings` scene (QnetGUIApp.swift:1000-1003) and IS movable, so the complaint is about sheets, not Settings.
findings.proposed_fix: Introduce `DSDialogWindow` in WindowSupport.swift as a thin wrapper over `AuxiliaryWindow.make` that hosts a `DSSheet` body in a titled, movable, non-modal `NSWindow` sized from its `DSSheetSize` (min/ideal/max already exist at DSSheet.swift:43-105; add matching `DS.Layout.Window.dialog*` NSSize accessors in DesignSystem.swift so no frame literal is written). Convert the four dialogs the user has to consult the canvas or the Shell for: `RunParameterSheet` (QnetGUIApp.swift:759-761), `TestSetParameterSheet` (:710-723), `SpectralConvergenceParameterSheet` (:728-740) and `GenerateRandomNetworkSheet` (:745-753). Keep them app-modal-free but single-instance (the `retained` static pattern at MethodChooserView.swift:700). Leave genuinely modal, must-answer sheets as sheets: `StartupDependencyCheckView` (:701) and the two parameter-editor sheets, which already have a modeless twin in the docked Inspector (InspectorPaneView.swift:37-38). `MenuContext.appSheetPresented` (WindowSupport.swift:208) gates canvas key equivalents while a sheet is up; a converted dialog must instead rely on the key-window check `MenuContext.keyWindowIsMain` (WindowSupport.swift:201) so tool letter shortcuts do not fire into the dialog's text fields — that mechanism already exists and already works for Help/Settings.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Run ▸ Run Monte Carlo… opens a titled window the user can drag anywhere, including onto a second display, while the canvas stays visible and interactive behind it. Typing a tool letter (e.g. "s") into one of its fields inserts the character rather than switching the canvas tool. Cancel and Run behave exactly as today, and the window remembers its position across launches via `setFrameAutosaveName`. Escape cancels. Only one instance opens per dialog.
findings.risk: Sheets currently guarantee that no second sheet and no tab switch can happen underneath them (`MenuContext.anySheetPresented`, WindowSupport.swift:217, consumed at WorkspaceCommands.swift:143, 150, 167, 182, 196…). A modeless dialog loses that guarantee, so the run closure must re-read the front editor at Run time rather than capturing it at open time — otherwise a run's status lines land in the wrong tab, which is the exact hazard the comment at WorkspaceCommands.swift:32-35 warns about.

findings.title: Rebalance the toolbar: six of eight default items are pane toggles and Run is absent
findings.user_impact: The toolbar of a numerical-analysis application leads with six window-management toggles and two canvas actions. The action the user came to perform — run a solver — is not there at all, only in a menu. The six toggles are undifferentiated `.primaryAction` icons with no grouping, so they read as a wall of similar glyphs and duplicate View ▸ Panes exactly.
findings.evidence: Nine `ToolbarItem(id:…)` entries at Sources/Qnet/ContentView.swift:231-302: straighten (231), fit (243), snap (253, hidden by default), then panes.palette (260), panes.status (267), panes.results (274), panes.inspector (281), panes.shell (288), panes.ai (295). All are `placement: .primaryAction`; none is a `ToolbarItemGroup` or `ControlGroup`. The Run menu, including `Run Comparison` on ⌘R and `Choose a Method…`, lives only in QnetCommands.swift:803-818.
findings.proposed_fix: Group the six pane toggles into one `ToolbarItemGroup(id: "panes", placement: .primaryAction)` rendered as a `ControlGroup` (a single segmented cluster, one visual unit), and add two leading items: a Run control whose primary action is `actions.runComparison()` (⌘R) with a menu of the enabled methods, and a `Workspace Presets` menu item exposing the four existing presets (WorkspaceCommands.swift:69-99). Keep every existing item id so a user's customized toolbar is not invalidated; a regrouped item changes rendering, not identity.
findings.acceptance_criteria: The default toolbar shows: Straighten, Zoom to Fit, a Run split-button, a Workspace Presets menu, and one segmented pane-toggle cluster. Clicking the Run button runs the same comparison ⌘R runs. All nine existing `ToolbarItem` ids still resolve, so an existing customized arrangement is preserved. Design lint passes (no literal SF Symbols, no frame literals).
findings.risk: Toolbar customization identity is stored by AppKit under the `toolbar(id: "qnet.main")` key; adding items is safe, but changing an existing item's id would silently reset a user's arrangement. Adding a Run item requires the same `!hasNetwork || sheetPresented` disabling QnetCommands.swift:810, 817 applies, or the button will launch a solver on an empty canvas.

findings.title: Auxiliary windows never set collectionBehavior, so they cannot appear beside a full-screened main window
findings.user_impact: A user working full-screen on a laptop who opens Qnet Help, the Method Chooser or the Network Model guide is pulled out of the full-screen space instead of getting a floating panel over their work. The same defect would afflict every detached pane window built on the same factory.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'collectionBehavior|fullScreen|toggleFullScreen' Sources/Qnet/*.swift` returns no hits at all. `AuxiliaryWindow.make` sets styleMask, tabbingMode, isExcludedFromWindowsMenu, isReleasedWhenClosed, titlebarAppearsTransparent, content size, min size and centring (Sources/Qnet/WindowSupport.swift:113-127) but never `collectionBehavior`, so every one of the six aux windows uses the AppKit default.
findings.proposed_fix: In `AuxiliaryWindow.make`, after line 122, insert `window.collectionBehavior.insert([.fullScreenAuxiliary, .moveToActiveSpace])` for panel-style windows. Expose it as a parameter (`fullScreenAuxiliary: Bool = true`) so a window that legitimately wants its own full-screen space — none today — can opt out. The Method Chooser, Network Model guide and any detached pane are the strongest cases: they are consulted while looking at the canvas.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Put the main window in full screen, then choose Help ▸ Qnet Help and Run ▸ Choose a Method…: both windows appear floating over the full-screen main window without switching spaces. Behaviour outside full screen is unchanged.
findings.risk: `.moveToActiveSpace` changes where a re-shown retained window appears for users who deliberately parked it on another space; if that matters, ship `.fullScreenAuxiliary` alone.

findings.title: FocusRouter cannot see a pane outside an NSSplitView and keeps only one handler slot per pane
findings.user_impact: Today this is latent; the moment any pane exists in a second window it becomes visible breakage — the pane's keyboard-focus rule never lights, `Window ▸ Focus <pane>` (⌃⌘1–6) silently does nothing, and ⌘F / ⌥⌘= route to the wrong place. It is also the reason a naive pop-out attempt would look broken on day one.
findings.evidence: `FocusRouter.paneRoot` walks up until it finds a view whose `superview is NSSplitView` and returns nil otherwise (Sources/Qnet/PaneChrome.swift:139-147) — in an `NSHostingController` window there is no NSSplitView, so `pane(containing:)` at PaneChrome.swift:149-156 never matches and `focusedPane` stays nil (PaneChrome.swift:158-167). The handler tables are one dictionary slot per pane (PaneChrome.swift:52-64), written in `onAppear` and set to nil in `onDisappear` — e.g. StatusLog.swift:299-320, ContentView.swift:1225-1235, InspectorPaneView.swift:119-128 — so during a detach the new host's `onAppear` and the old pane's `onDisappear` race, and the loser nils a live handler.
findings.proposed_fix: (a) In `paneRoot`, fall back to the marker's `window?.contentView` when no NSSplitView ancestor is found, so a pane hosted directly in a window still resolves a root. (b) Give the four setter families an owner token: `func setFocusHandler(_ pane:, owner: ObjectIdentifier, _ handler:)` and have the clearing call be a no-op unless the stored owner matches — the standard fix for the SwiftUI onAppear/onDisappear ordering race. (c) Make `WorkspaceCommands` Focus actions (WorkspaceCommands.swift:202-257) order a detached pane's window front before calling `FocusRouter.shared.focus(_:)`.
findings.acceptance_criteria: With the Shell docked, ⌃⌘3 focuses it and the header shows the 2-pt accent rule, exactly as today. With the Shell detached, ⌃⌘3 brings the detached window forward, focuses the terminal, and lights its header rule. Toggling a pane off and on twice in a row leaves ⌘F and ⌥⌘=/⌥⌘− still routed to it (regression test for the handler race).
findings.risk: Changing `paneRoot`'s fallback widens what counts as a pane root; `firstFocusable(in:)` (PaneChrome.swift:183-195) already skips split views and hosting containers, but with a whole contentView as root it may pick a different first responder than intended for a docked pane — keep the NSSplitView branch first so docked behaviour is byte-identical.

findings.title: Minimum window height plus chrome exceeds the usable height of an 800-pt display
findings.user_impact: On a 1280×800 external display (or a 1440×900 with the Dock on the bottom edge), the main window cannot be shown in full: macOS will either clip it behind the Dock or refuse the user's attempt to shrink it. A user on a projector or an older second monitor cannot get a workable window.
findings.evidence: `.frame(minWidth: DS.Layout.Window.mainMinWidth, minHeight: DS.Layout.Window.mainMinHeight)` at Sources/Qnet/ContentView.swift:217-218, with `mainMinHeight = 720` at DesignSystem.swift:1167; that is content height, below a unified titlebar+toolbar (`.windowToolbarStyle(.unified)`, QnetGUIApp.swift:985) of roughly 52 pt, giving a hard floor near 772 pt. An 800-pt screen has ~776 pt of `visibleFrame` with the menu bar alone and ~706 pt with the Dock. The 720 floor is itself only just above the sum of the row minimums (320 + 192 + 192 = 704, DesignSystem.swift:1148-1151).
findings.proposed_fix: Lower `mainMinHeight` to the true structural floor — the sum of the minimum heights of the rows that are actually present — by making the min-height conditional in ContentView rather than a constant: when the bottom row or Results is hidden, the window should legitimately be allowed to shrink. Concretely, compute a `contentMinHeight` from `outerPanes` (ContentView.swift:49-55) using the same `canvasRowMinHeight`/`bottomRowMinHeight` tokens, and apply that instead of the flat `Window.mainMinHeight`. Keep `mainMinWidth = 1000` (the width floor is genuine: 152 + 496 + 288 + dividers ≈ 938, DesignSystem.swift:1142-1146).
findings.acceptance_criteria: On a display whose `visibleFrame` height is 706 pt, the main window can be resized to fit entirely on screen with at least the canvas and one other pane visible. With every pane shown, the min height is still the honest sum of the row minimums, and no row is squeezed below its own minimum.
findings.risk: A conditional min height re-evaluates on every pane toggle; if the window is already at the old minimum, hiding a pane will not shrink it (AppKit does not shrink windows on a min-size change) — acceptable, but the window will now allow a manual shrink where it previously refused.

findings.title: The Settings window's frame is not persisted the way every other window's is
findings.user_impact: Five auxiliary windows and the main window come back at the size and position the user left them; the Settings window does not participate in the app's own frame-persistence scheme, so a user who widens Settings to read a long solver-parameter form has to widen it again next time.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'setFrameAutosaveName' Sources/Qnet/*.swift` yields exactly five hits — DSGallery.swift:733, MethodChooserView.swift:716, NetworkModelGuideView.swift:378, QnetHelpWindow.swift:966, ReleaseNotesWindow.swift:254 — plus the comment at ContentView.swift:1566. `SettingsView` applies only a size band (`.frame(minWidth:idealWidth:minHeight:idealHeight:)` at SettingsView.swift:186-189) and a tagger that exists solely to commit fields on close (SettingsComponents.swift:241-297); `WindowFrameAutosave` is attached to the main window only (ContentView.swift:1568).
findings.proposed_fix: Attach the app's existing `WindowFrameAutosave(name: "QnetSettingsWindow")` as a `.background` on `SettingsView`'s root, next to the existing `SettingsWindowTagger()` at SettingsView.swift:194. It already retries until `view.window` exists (ContentView.swift:1600-1613) and clamps to visible screens (ContentView.swift:1663-1676), so no new machinery is needed — this is a one-line reuse.

findings.risk: `WindowFrameAutosave.save()` ignores frames under 200×200 (ContentView.swift:1651), so a transiently small Settings window will not poison the stored value. The tagger's `willClose` first-responder resign (SettingsComponents.swift:289-291) and the autosave's `willClose` save both fire; order is irrelevant since they touch different state.

dimension: The embedded interactive shell (SwiftTerm) as the centrepiece of the GUI — prominence, terminal capability, run lifecycle feedback, typing/safety, coherence with StatusLog + ResultsWorkspace, readability, and getting a result table out.

already_good.what: Run cancellation is genuinely production-grade: Stop is live from millisecond zero (the model re-reads the pid every 100 ms for a second before giving up), signals the wrapper's process *group* (never Qnet's own), escalates SIGINT → SIGTERM at 1.5 s → SIGKILL at 3 s, and only retires the job once the pid is demonstrably gone, so a SIGKILLed wrapper that never ran its EXIT trap cannot leave the indicator ticking. Do not rebuild this.
already_good.evidence: Sources/Qnet/TerminalModel.swift:624-676 (cancelActiveRun + retry task), :500-527 (tickRun escalation/deadline), :678-691 (signalActiveRun group guard), :108-116 (cancelEscalateAfter/cancelDeadline)

already_good.what: Single-flight run ownership with per-run UUID-scoped coordination files (done/pid/status/output). A second launch is refused with a message naming the owning tab rather than silently replacing the poller, and every lifecycle/diagnostic message is routed to the *originating* editor captured at launch, not to whatever tab is active when the poll tick fires.
The completion file is written from an EXIT trap rather than the last line of the wrapper, so ⌃C in the shell or Stop Run still retires the status-bar indicator and still reports 130.
already_good.evidence: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5789-5801 (runScript scriptBody trap), Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:7474 (silentScript same trap)

already_good.what: Determinate progress is real, not decorative: solvers write `<total>\n` then one byte per unit to a `-P` file; the shell draws an ANSI bar from that file and TerminalModel polls the *same* file so the canvas status bar shows the same percentage. When no total is available it deliberately falls back to an indeterminate spinner instead of a bar that never moves, and withSpinner covers opaque solvers with elapsed time.

Verbatim byte-stream transcript capture and replay across launches — including the pre-sizing to 120×30 so replay does not wrap at MINIMUM_COLS, the ESC[?1049l / ESC[?2004l / ESC[?25h / ESC[0m reset for a session force-killed inside a full-screen program, the lock-protected PendingByteBuffer so the last bytes before ⌘Q are not stranded behind an actor hop, and re-seeding the capture buffer with what was replayed.

The shell process survives every layout change. TerminalModel caches the AppKit host view and SwiftTermView merely re-parents it, so collapsing the AI pane, hiding the Shell pane or restructuring the split never restarts the shell or loses scrollback. This is exactly the property a pop-out window would need.

External overlay scrollers (vertical + horizontal) hand-built to track SwiftTerm's own scroll state, with NSScrollView-style fade-in/fade-out on DS.Motion durations, hover-persist tracking areas, and a local wheel monitor that turns predominantly-horizontal trackpad deltas into panning because SwiftTerm's scrollWheel is not overridable.
ANSI palette is design-system driven for both grounds plus a classic green-on-black mode, re-applied on appearance change because SwiftTerm resolves dynamic NSColors at assignment time.

Solver stderr is not thrown away: a non-zero exit dumps stderr into the shell *and* appends a sentinel-delimited record to a per-run inbox that surfaces in the originating tab's Status pane; a clean exit still greps stderr for the documented stability warnings (Dai–Vande Vate, Bramson, Kumar–Seidman, divergence) and surfaces those too.

Shell pane header condenses correctly: below DS.Layout.headerCondenseWidthWide the font family and size steppers fold into one overflow menu instead of crushing the title and path; Copy confirms in the status log with a character count and a 1 s checkmark; the terminal view carries a real VoiceOver role, label and help.

Text-size and focus routing already work for the shell: ⌃` / ⌃⌘3 reveal-then-focus it, ⌥⌘= / ⌥⌘− route to the terminal font through FocusRouter with correct enablement at the clamp bounds, and the font family/size persist across launches.

ResultOutputParser strips ANSI and collapses \r before matching, and parses by semantic row name rather than column position — so the progress-bar redraws in the captured stream do not corrupt measurement extraction.

With nodes selected on the canvas AND a shell selection, ⌘C while the Shell is focused copies the shell text; ⌘C while the canvas is focused copies the nodes. Watch that observing `TerminalModel` in QnetCommands does not add a redraw storm — the model publishes runElapsed every 500 ms during a run, so read `hasSelection` through a non-@Published accessor or gate on `focusedPane` first.

findings.title: Wide solver tables hard-wrap because nothing reports their width to the terminal
findings.user_impact: The comparison table is the single most important thing the app prints, and it is the output most likely to be destroyed. `minTerminalWidth` — the whole mechanism that widens the terminal view and engages the horizontal scroller so long lines stay on one line — is fed by exactly two call sites, both of them Swift-generated reports (Network Primitives, Analyze Network). No solver run ever calls it. A Run Comparison table is roughly `label + 5 columns × (value + “ (+12.3%)”)` ≈ 95–110 columns; in the default layout the Shell is ~745 pt wide ⇒ ~100 columns at 12 pt, and narrower the moment the user widens the AI pane or the Inspector. Every row then wraps mid-number and the aligned table becomes an unreadable zig-zag, with no scrollbar offered because `desiredMinWidth` is still 0.
findings.evidence: Only callers: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:6070 and :6125 (formatNetworkPrimitives / formatNetworkAnalysis). Mechanism: Sources/Qnet/TerminalModel.swift:821-848 (reportLongestLineChars → recomputeMinTerminalWidth), consumed at Sources/Qnet/TerminalConsoleView.swift:585-586 and :436-460 (`let targetWidth = max(desiredMinWidth, visibleWidth)`). Table width is decided at runtime inside awk, not in Swift: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5434-5446 (per-column max width + 2-space gutter). Pane geometry: Sources/Qnet/DesignSystem.swift:1150-1151 (bottomRowIdealHeight 248) and Sources/Qnet/AppSettings.swift:482-492 (AI pane default 255 pt).
findings.proposed_fix: Measure the width from the byte stream rather than from Swift. In `TerminalModel.appendCapturedBytes` (Sources/Qnet/TerminalModel.swift:838-846) maintain a running current-line character count: reset on `\n` and on `\r`, ignore CSI/OSC escape sequences with a tiny 3-state scanner (ESC → `[` → consume until a byte in 0x40…0x7E), and call the existing `reportLongestLineChars` on each line break. Because `reportLongestLineChars` already keeps a monotonic peak and is reset by `clearTerminal()`/`restart()`, no other change is needed and the progress-bar redraws (which are \r-terminated and full of CSI) contribute nothing. Optionally add a Shell header toggle “Fit Width / Don’t Wrap” bound to whether `desiredMinWidth` is honoured, so a user who prefers wrapping can have it.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Run Comparison on a 6-station network with the Shell pane narrowed to ~500 pt: the table prints with every row on one physical line and the horizontal overlay scroller becomes enabled and scrolls the full table into view. Clear Shell (⌘K) retracts the scroller. Changing the shell font size re-computes the width (existing `recomputeMinTerminalWidth` path). No measurable typing latency in the shell (the scanner is O(bytes) with no allocation).
findings.risk: `appendCapturedBytes` runs on SwiftTerm’s pty reader path (called from `dataReceived`, Sources/Qnet/TerminalConsoleView.swift:29-32) — keep the scanner allocation-free and do not touch main-actor state from it; today the reader writes into the lock-protected `pendingBytes` and only the main actor drains, so the counter must live on whichever side actually runs. Growing `desiredMinWidth` changes SwiftTerm’s cols, which fires `sizeChanged` → `layoutTerminal`; verify no feedback loop when the pane is resized during output.

findings.title: Give the Shell a real centrepiece layout: a Shell-dominant workspace preset, a pop-out window, and stop force-opening Results on top of it
findings.user_impact: Today the Shell is a 248-pt-tall strip at the bottom of the window sharing its row with the AI pane (255 pt), i.e. about 14 visible text rows and ~100 columns at the 1000×720 minimum window. A comparison table for 5 stations with ρ/Γ/sojourn/E[Q] rows is ~25 lines plus two banner lines — it cannot be seen at once. And the moment a run *starts*, ContentView force-shows the Results pane, stealing another 248 pt from exactly the pane whose output is arriving. There is no “Shell” workspace preset (the closest, “Run and Diagnose”, still keeps Results and Status), no way to maximise the pane, and no way to detach it into its own window the way MATLAB detaches a panel.

(c) Add Window ▸ Shell ▸ “Open Shell in a Window” using the existing `AuxiliaryWindow.make(id:"shell", …)`, whose root hosts `SwiftTermView`; because `TerminalModel.hostView` is a cached, re-parentable NSView the shell process is untouched — but the docked pane MUST be hidden while the window is open (set `appSettings.shellPaneVisible = false` on open, restore on close) since only one `attachHost` target may own the view at a time.

Starting a run with Results hidden and Shell visible does not resize the Shell. findings.title: Strip ANSI and collapse progress-bar redraws before storing rawOutput — the Results “Solver Transcript” is currently unreadable and the archive bloats
findings.user_impact: `terminal.lastRunOutput` is the verbatim tee of the wrapper’s stdout, escape codes and all. It is stored on every run record and shown in the Results workspace as `Text(rawOutput)` with a “Copy Transcript” button. So the user opens Solver Transcript and sees literal `ESC[7m`/`ESC[27m`/`\r ESC[K` noise, with every 200 ms progress-bar redraw stacked as a separate line, and Copy Transcript puts that on the clipboard. Every one of those redraws is also JSON-encoded into `results-v1.json`, which is rewritten in full on every single mutation — a 10-minute run contributes ~3,000 redraw lines (~270 KB) per record, and there is no record cap.

String(contentsOfFile: runOutputPath…)`, no normalisation) fed by the tee at Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5789-5801. Stored raw: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5883, :5890, :5903, :5913, :5920 → Sources/Qnet/ResultsWorkspace.swift:535, :556, :572, :585. Displayed raw: Sources/Qnet/ResultsWorkspace.swift:1310-1342 (`Text(rawOutput)`, `pasteboard.setString(rawOutput…)`). Persisted on every mutate: Sources/Qnet/ResultsWorkspace.swift:615-635. The cleaner already exists but is private to the parser: Sources/Qnet/ResultOutputParser.swift:688-697. Redraw source: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5660-5680 (`printf '\r\033[K…'` every 0.2 s).

Call it once in `finalizeStructuredResult` before handing `raw` to `ResultsStore` (Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5878-5925), so both the stored archive and the Results transcript view get clean text. Leave the parser’s own internal normalisation as is; it is already correct.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Run a simulation with a progress bar, open Results ▸ Solver Transcript: no `ESC[` sequences are visible, the progress bar appears as one completed line, and the visible text matches what the Shell shows. Copy Transcript pastes the same clean text into TextEdit. `results-v1.json` for that run is an order of magnitude smaller than before. `validation/result_output_parser/` still compiles and passes (the headless check builds ResultOutputParser.swift against stubs.swift — do not add a dependency to that file).
findings.risk: validation/result_output_parser compiles ResultOutputParser.swift + stubs.swift + main.swift in isolation (CLAUDE.md “Headless Swift unit checks”); adding any new import or type reference to that file breaks the check until the stub grows. Keep the new function dependency-free (Foundation only). Also confirm the `\r`-collapse does not eat legitimate content in solvers that use \r for anything but redraws.

findings.title: Keep machine sentinel lines out of the human-facing shell
findings.user_impact: Python solvers print their machine-readable channel straight into the pane that is supposed to be the centrepiece. Running Regenerative Monte Carlo dumps a block headed “Per-node metrics (QNET_NODE_METRIC_V1):” followed by one ~150-character line per node × 4 metrics, each carrying a raw node UUID (`QNET_NODE_METRIC_V1 node_id=1F2E…-… metric=utilization class_id=… estimate=… standard_error=… ci_confidence=… ci_low=… ci_high=… ci_half_width=… effective_cycles=…`). A finite comparison that loses its CTMC column prints `QNET_COMPARISON_STATUS_V1 partial=yes successful=other failed=ctmc`. QBD prints `QNET_QBD_METRIC_V1 …`. These lines are for `ResultOutputParser`, they wrap catastrophically in a 100-column pane, and to a user they read as the program leaking its internals.
findings.evidence: Emitted to stdout: infinite/regenerative_mc/regenerative_mc.py:1751 and following, infinite/matrix_analytic/qbd_solver.py:1067-1071; Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:4996-4997 (`printf 'QNET_COMPARISON_STATUS_V1 partial=yes…'`). Consumed by Sources/Qnet/ResultOutputParser.swift:110-135 (regenerativeMetricRow, qbdMetricRow, qbdEvidenceRow, mlmcStatusRow). Python runners pipe solver stdout straight through with no formatter, unlike C runners which go through the awk table: compare Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:1799-1803 (`solve` → withSpinner → runScript, no format step) with :3486-3498 (QNA → singleMethodFormatCmd).
findings.proposed_fix: Split the machine channel from the display channel in the wrapper, not in the solvers. In the Python runners, tee stdout to the run’s capture file (which is what `ResultOutputParser` reads via `lastRunOutput`) but filter the terminal view with a one-line `grep -v '^QNET_[A-Z_]*_V1 '` — i.e. wrap the solver invocation as `{ solve; } | tee -a "$QNET_RAW" | grep -v …`. Since `runScript` already tees the whole wrapper to `handle.outputPath` (Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5789-5801), the cheapest correct shape is to keep the tee where it is and instead have the *display* side filter: change the wrapper’s final stage from `2>&1 | tee "outputPath"` to `2>&1 | tee "outputPath" | grep -v -e '^QNET_[A-Z0-9_]*_V1 ' -e '^Per-node metrics (QNET'`. Nothing the parser needs is lost, because the parser reads the tee’d file, not the terminal.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Run Regenerative Monte Carlo: the Shell shows the human summary and no `QNET_*_V1` line; the Results record for that run still contains every per-node measurement with its standard error and CI (proving the parser still saw the sentinels). Same for QBD and for a finite comparison that drops the CTMC column. `validation/gui_runtime_contracts.sh` still passes — it greps for `QNET_METHOD_FAILURE_V1 method=ctmc` in QnetGUIApp.swift, which this change leaves textually intact.
findings.risk: gui_runtime_contracts.sh asserts exact strings in the wrapper region (`trap cleanup_qnet_solver_inputs EXIT`, `trap 'exit 130' INT TERM`, the 8 `commandWithCleanup` call sites, `QNET_METHOD_FAILURE_V1 method=ctmc`). Editing the tee line in runScript/silentScript is not covered by any of those greps, but adding a pipeline stage changes `PIPESTATUS[0]` semantics — the exit code is read as `_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}` and must keep pointing at the brace group, so append the grep AFTER the existing tee and re-verify a deliberately failing solver still reports its real exit code in the status bar.

findings.title: Print a run header in the Shell so a scrollback of six runs is readable
findings.user_impact: Runs are indistinguishable in the scrollback. `runScript` deliberately erases the echoed `bash /tmp/BNET_run_<uuid>.sh` line, so the user cannot even see that a command was issued, let alone which method, on which network, with what parameters, at what time. What survives is `[Threads] Single-threaded (analytical solver)`, a spinner line, a table, and `Elapsed time: 0.412s`. Scroll up past three runs and there is no way to tell which table belongs to which method or which network tab — the very provenance the Results workspace records is absent from the pane the user is reading. Nothing separates one run from the next either.

What is printed instead: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:7517-7524 (threadCountBanner), :5090-5112 (regimeHeader), :5074-5082 (tractabilityHeader) — none names the method, the network, the tab or the time. Use `TerminalModel.displayLabel(forRunLabel:)` (Sources/Qnet/TerminalModel.swift:352-369) for the human name so the shell, the status bar and the Stop menu item all say the same word. Keep the `\033[A\033[2K` erase — the banner replaces the echoed command as the visible marker.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Run QNA, then Spectral, then Run Comparison on two different tabs. Scrolling back through the Shell, each run is introduced by a rule naming the method, the network title and the wall-clock time, and its parameters. The banner text matches the method name shown in the canvas status bar’s “Last run” segment and in the Results workspace row for the same run. No duplicate banner appears for runs that already print regimeHeader/tractabilityHeader.
findings.risk: Both wrapper bodies are dense shell strings; a quoting error here breaks every solver launch. Escape `%` and `'` in the title exactly as `withProgress` does (Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5638-5641) — network titles are user-supplied. gui_runtime_contracts.sh does not grep the runScript body, but verify the added `printf` does not disturb `_t0` capture or the `PIPESTATUS[0]` read.

findings.title: Make a result table copyable into a spreadsheet — add “Copy Last Run as TSV” and “Save Shell Output…”
findings.user_impact: Getting a table out of the terminal into Excel or a paper is bad today. The awk formatter pads columns with spaces (`printf "%-*s  "`), SwiftTerm has no rectangular/column selection, and the only copy path is the header button, which yields space-padded text plus the `(+12.3%)` delta suffixes glued to each value — pasting that into Numbers or Excel gives one column that must be run through Text-to-Columns and then hand-cleaned. There is no “Save Shell Output…” at all: File ▸ Export offers Diagram PDF/PNG, three solver inputs, and the Status Log, but nothing for the run output the user actually publishes. The structured escape hatch (Results ▸ Copy CSV) exists but lives in a different pane the user may have closed, and it is not offered anywhere near the shell.
findings.evidence: Space padding: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5434-5446. Delta suffix baked into the cell: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5308 (`sprintf("%s (%+.1f%%)", …)`). Copy path: Sources/Qnet/ContentView.swift:1183-1190 → Sources/Qnet/TerminalModel.swift:310-330 (plain string, selection or whole buffer). No rectangular selection in the widget: Vendor/SwiftTerm/Sources/SwiftTerm/SelectionService.swift:91-536 exposes only linear start/extend/selectAll. No shell export: Sources/Qnet/QnetCommands.swift:268-312 (Export submenu). Existing structured exporter that should be surfaced: Sources/Qnet/ResultsWorkspace.swift:694-780 (`ResultsExport.csv`) and :763-772 (`copyCSV`).
findings.proposed_fix: Two additions, both reusing what exists. (a) Add a Shell-header menu item and a File ▸ Export item “Last Run Output…” that writes `terminal.lastRunOutput` (sanitised by the same helper as the Results-transcript fix) to a `.txt`, modelled line-for-line on `StatusLogExport.save` (Sources/Qnet/StatusLogExport.swift:22-51) including the “Saved N … to <path>” status-log confirmation. (b) Add “Copy Last Run as TSV” in the Shell header overflow menu that calls `ResultsExport.copyCSV(records:[record for terminal.lastRunSummary?.id], …)` with a TSV variant — the record already carries station, metric, estimate, unit, SE, CI, seed and parameters as typed fields, so no scraping is involved and the result pastes into a spreadsheet as real columns.
findings.acceptance_criteria: After a Run Comparison, Shell header ▸ ⋯ ▸ Copy Last Run as TSV then ⌘V in Numbers produces a grid with one row per (station, metric) and separate numeric columns — no manual Text-to-Columns. File ▸ Export ▸ Last Run Output… writes a .txt whose content matches the Shell verbatim minus escape codes, and the Status pane logs the destination path. Both items are disabled with an explanatory tooltip when no run has completed.
findings.risk: `lastRunSummary` is replaced by the next run (Sources/Qnet/TerminalModel.swift:707-716), so “Last Run” must be resolved through `ResultsStore.record(id:)` rather than held, or the export silently targets the wrong run. `ResultsExport.csv` writes raw `String(estimate)` for numbers (Sources/Qnet/ResultsWorkspace.swift:769-771) — the decimal-places setting is not applied there, which is a separate consistency issue; do not let this finding’s fix entrench it.

findings.title: Add a right-click context menu to the terminal
findings.user_impact: Right-clicking anywhere in the Shell does nothing. Neither SwiftTerm nor Qnet installs a menu, so the muscle-memory route to Copy / Paste / Select All / Clear / Find — the first thing anyone tries in Terminal.app or iTerm — is dead. Every one of those actions exists but is reachable only from the pane header’s icon row or a menu-bar path the user has to learn.

The actions all exist: Sources/Qnet/TerminalModel.swift:310 (copySelectionOrAll), :332 (showFind), :266 (clearTerminal), :340 (scrollToBottom); SwiftTerm supplies `paste(_:)` and `selectAll(_:)` (Vendor/SwiftTerm/Sources/SwiftTerm/Mac/MacTerminalView.swift:1876-1898).

Route the items to `TerminalModel` through the existing weak `model` reference on `TerminalHostView`. Titles must match the pane header and the Window ▸ Shell menu word-for-word.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Right-click over the terminal with a selection: Copy is enabled and copies the selection; with no selection Copy is disabled. Paste inserts the clipboard at the prompt. Clear Shell empties the pane and the prompt redraws. Item titles are identical to the corresponding pane-header tooltips and Window ▸ Shell items. design_lint passes (this is AppKit menu construction, outside the SwiftUI Divider() rule — verify the lint’s menu-scope brace tracking is not tripped).
findings.risk: The design lint replaces `Divider()` outside a menu builder with `DSRule()` and tracks menu scope by brace depth (validation/design_lint.sh header); an NSMenu built in AppKit uses `NSMenuItem.separator()` and is unaffected, but confirm before assuming. Also ensure the menu does not steal right-click while SwiftTerm mouse reporting is active (a full-screen program like `htop` wants the raw event).

findings.title: Wire ⌘G / ⇧⌘G to the shell find bar and give it a match count

The bar itself is vendored AppKit chrome that looks nothing like the rest of the app (a `.popover` NSVisualEffectView with a hard-coded 8-pt radius, `Aa` / `.*` / `Word` checkboxes) and shows no “3 of 17” counter, so the user cannot tell whether a search matched at all or has wrapped.
findings.evidence: Shell registers only a find handler, never a step handler: Sources/Qnet/ContentView.swift:1234; step routing at Sources/Qnet/QnetCommands.swift:603-611 → Sources/Qnet/PaneChrome.swift:125-134 (`canStepFind` false when `findStepHandlers[pane] == nil`). SwiftTerm already supports it: Vendor/SwiftTerm/Sources/SwiftTerm/Mac/MacTerminalView.swift:1726-1745 (`.nextMatch` / `.previousMatch`) and Vendor/SwiftTerm/Sources/SwiftTerm/TerminalViewSearch.swift:19-55 (`findNext` / `findPrevious` / `clearSearch`). Bar chrome: Vendor/SwiftTerm/Sources/SwiftTerm/Mac/MacFindBarView.swift:51-56 and :17-22 (no counter label anywhere in the file). Contrast the DS search field used by every other pane: Sources/Qnet/StatusLog.swift:402-411 (DSSearchField with a `status:` readout).

Better: replace the vendored bar entirely with a `DSSearchField` in a Qnet-owned strip under the Shell header (the same shape the Status pane uses), driving `terminalView.findNext/findPrevious` directly from `TerminalViewSearch` and reporting a match count in the field’s `status:` slot — that also removes the last non-DS chrome from the pane.

If the DS bar replacement is done: the field matches the Status pane’s search field visually, shows “n of m”, and Escape closes it without closing the window. design_lint passes.

Do not edit Vendor/SwiftTerm.

findings.title: Stop persisting the shell transcript to UserDefaults without an opt-out
findings.user_impact: Up to 1 MiB of the terminal’s raw byte stream is written to the app’s preferences plist at quit and replayed on the next launch. Because it is captured from the pty, it contains the shell’s *echo* of everything the user typed — so an `export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=…` typed at the prompt, a token pasted into a curl command, or a private path is stored in cleartext in ~/Library/Preferences and re-rendered on screen at the next launch. There is no setting to disable transcript persistence, no “clear saved transcript” separate from a full Restart Shell, and the Settings pane for the shell offers only font, size and the classic theme.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/TerminalModel.swift:190-203 (`savedRawBytesKey`, `maxCapturedBytes = 1_048_576`), :869-901 (`saveTranscript` → `UserDefaults.standard.set(data, forKey:)` + `synchronize()`), :903-915 (loaders), replay at Sources/Qnet/TerminalConsoleView.swift:184-243. Capture source is the pty stream including echo: Sources/Qnet/TerminalConsoleView.swift:29-32 (`dataReceived`) → Sources/Qnet/TerminalModel.swift:838-846. Only escape hatch today is destructive: Sources/Qnet/WorkspaceCommands.swift:368-374 (Restart Shell… “the saved transcript will not be restored”). Settings offer nothing: Sources/Qnet/SettingsView.swift:2048-2076.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `shell.persistTranscript` (default on, so behaviour is unchanged for existing users) to `AppSettings.Defaults` and the Interactive Shell settings pane beside the font controls, with an explicit caption saying the transcript includes typed commands and is stored in the app’s preferences. Gate `saveTranscript()` on it and clear the stored blob when it is switched off (`TerminalModel.clearSavedTranscript()` already exists, Sources/Qnet/TerminalModel.swift:917-920). Add a plain “Forget Saved Transcript” button that calls it without restarting the shell. Register the new key in the settings search haystack (Sources/Qnet/SettingsView.swift:503-505) so it is findable.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Settings ▸ Interactive Shell Window shows a “Restore previous session’s shell output” toggle and a “Forget Saved Transcript” button. Turning the toggle off removes the `shell.savedRawBytes` key immediately (verifiable with `defaults read`) and the next launch opens a clean shell. With it on, behaviour is byte-identical to today. The new key appears in Settings search for “transcript”, “privacy”, “history”. `AppSettings` reset restores the default.
findings.risk: AppSettings registers defaults in a table (Sources/Qnet/AppSettings.swift:661-674) that the settings audit cross-checks; add the key in both places or the audit fails. Do not change `maxCapturedBytes` — the replay path and the trim in `appendCapturedBytes` are tuned to it.

findings.title: Show run state in the Shell pane itself, not only in the canvas status bar
findings.user_impact: When the Shell is where the user is looking, the run’s identity, progress percentage, elapsed clock and Stop button are somewhere else entirely — in the status bar at the bottom of the *canvas* column. The Shell header shows only a green/red dot for “shell process alive” and the current directory. During a long solve the user watching the terminal sees an ASCII bar with no method name and no way to stop it without moving the pointer across the window; if the Shell is popped out (once that exists) or the window is tall, the indicator is far away. The header is also where a “Stop” belongs by convention.
findings.evidence: Run segment lives in CanvasStatusBar: Sources/Qnet/ContentView.swift:920-1010 (`runSegment`, progress, elapsed clock, Stop button). Shell header contents: Sources/Qnet/ContentView.swift:1142-1209 — process dot, path, optional Restart, then Scroll to Bottom / Find / Copy / font / Clear / Restart. No reference to `terminal.activeRun`, `runProgress`, `runElapsed` or `canCancelRun` anywhere in TerminalPaneView.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a compact run indicator to the Shell’s `DSSectionHeader` leading slot, shown only while `terminal.activeRun != nil`: the run’s display label, `TerminalRunSummary.clock(runElapsed)`, a small determinate `ProgressView` when `runProgress != nil`, and a destructive Stop `DSIconButton` reusing the same action and the same help text as `CanvasStatusBar.stopRun()`. Reuse `TerminalRunSummary.clock` and `displayLabel(forRunLabel:)` so the two indicators cannot drift. Fade it with `.transition(.opacity)` and `dsAnimation(DS.Motion.quick, …)` as the existing Restart button does.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Start a long run: the Shell header shows “Spectral · 0:07 · [bar] · Stop” and the canvas status bar shows the same label, percentage and elapsed value at all times. Clicking Stop in the header produces exactly the same status-log line as Stop in the status bar. When idle the header returns to dot + path with no layout jump. Header still condenses correctly below DS.Layout.headerCondenseWidthWide (the run indicator must be the first thing dropped, not the title).
findings.risk: `TerminalModel` publishes `runElapsed` every 500 ms; the Shell pane already observes the model, so this adds a header re-render at that cadence — keep the indicator in its own small subview so SwiftUI does not re-evaluate the whole pane (and, critically, does not churn `SwiftTermView.updateNSView`, which re-runs `attachHost` and `layoutTerminal` on every pass).

findings.title: Guard sendCommand against a busy or non-prompt shell
findings.user_impact: Every solver launch is *typed into* the interactive shell. If the user has a half-typed command at the prompt, or is inside `less`, `vim`, `python`, or their own long-running job, the launcher appends `bash "/tmp/BNET_run_<uuid>.sh\n"` to that program’s stdin. The result ranges from a mangled command line to text inserted into a file being edited. `beginRun` only prevents a second *Qnet* run; it knows nothing about what the user is doing. The codebase already anticipates this — the cancel path has a dedicated message for “the shell is busy with something typed by hand” — but nothing prevents it. Additionally, the wrapper’s first act is `printf '\033[A\033[2K'`, which erases the line above; if the shell was not sitting at a fresh prompt, that erases a line of the user’s own output.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/TerminalModel.swift:774-778 (`sendCommand` writes bytes unconditionally, no state check); acknowledgement of the hazard at Sources/Qnet/TerminalModel.swift:655-661. Launch sites: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5836 (`terminalModel.sendCommand("bash \"…\"")`) and 8 `sendCommand(script)` sites (:1753, :2528, :2609, :2717, :2803, :3201, :6072, :6127). Line erase: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5789-5790 and :7474.
findings.proposed_fix: Before typing, detect that the shell is at an idle prompt. Two cheap, complementary signals: (a) SwiftTerm reports whether it is in alt-screen / a full-screen application — refuse and warn if so; (b) track whether any bytes have arrived from the pty in the last ~150 ms and whether the current row is non-empty to the left of the cursor. When the check fails, do not launch: call `failRunToLaunch` with an actionable message (“The Shell is busy — finish or interrupt what is running there first”) so the status bar does not wait for a completion file that will never be written, and beep as the existing refusal does. Also send a leading `\r\x15` (kill-line) before the command so a half-typed line is cleared rather than concatenated, which removes the most common case entirely.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Type `echo hel` at the prompt without pressing Return, then Run ▸ QNA: the run either launches cleanly (partial line discarded) or is refused with a status-log message naming the reason — it never produces `echo helbash /tmp/…`. Start `cat` (or `less`) in the shell, then Run ▸ QNA: the run is refused with an actionable message, the status bar returns to Idle rather than spinning, and no text is injected into `cat`. Normal launches from an idle prompt are unchanged.
findings.risk: `failRunToLaunch` requires the handle to still own the run (Sources/Qnet/TerminalModel.swift:494-498) — call it before any `sendCommand`, and make sure the ResultsStore record registered by `registerStructuredResult` (Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5827) is failed too, or the Results workspace keeps a permanently ‘running’ row. A false positive on the busy check would block legitimate launches, so bias the heuristic toward launching.

findings.title: Do not let printing a Help topic to the Shell consume the single run slot
findings.user_impact: Help ▸ (any algorithm topic) with the destination set to “Shell pane (plain text)” goes through `runScript`, which calls `beginRun`. While a solver is running, asking for help therefore beeps and logs “Network Primitives was not started because Spectral is already running for “Untitled”. Stop or wait for that run first.” — refusing to show documentation because a computation is in flight. It also makes the canvas status bar say “Running <help topic>…” and briefly claim a solver is executing when the app is only `cat`ing a text file.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5507-5523 (`printHelpToTerminal` → `runScript(command, label: label)`), called from :6163 (Help topics) and :942 (Settings ▸ Performance Hints). Refusal path: Sources/Qnet/TerminalModel.swift:414-421. Destination enum: Sources/Qnet/HelpOutputDestination.swift:18-38.
findings.proposed_fix: Give `printHelpToTerminal` a non-run path: write the temp file as today, then call `terminalModel.sendCommand("cat …; rm -f …")` directly without `beginRun`, so no completion file, no pid file, no status-bar claim and no lock. Keep the run-slot path only for things that actually execute a solver. If the busy-shell guard from the previous finding lands, reuse it here so help is queued or refused politely rather than injected into a running solver’s stdin.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Start a long solver run, then choose a Help topic with the Shell destination: the help text is refused *or* printed after the run, but never with the message “… was not started because …”, and the status bar keeps showing the solver’s name and progress throughout. With no run active, help printing behaves exactly as today.
findings.risk: If help output is sent while a solver is writing to the shell, the two streams interleave. Prefer refusing with a clear message over interleaving; do not silently drop the request.

findings.title: Start the shell in a meaningful directory instead of “/”
findings.user_impact: The Shell’s working directory is `FileManager.default.currentDirectoryPath`. For a bundled `Qnet.app` launched from Finder that is `/`, so the header proudly reports “Current directory: /” and the user’s first `ls` shows the root filesystem. A shell that is meant to be the centrepiece of a modelling tool should open where the user’s work is — next to the open .bnet document, or the home directory.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/ContentView.swift:26-28 (`workspaceURL`), passed to `TerminalPaneView(workingDirectory:)` at :179 and to `startProcess(currentDirectory:)` at Sources/Qnet/TerminalConsoleView.swift:150-155. No `chdir` anywhere in Sources/Qnet (only reads of `currentDirectoryPath` at QnetGUIApp.swift:1424 and SolverRuntimeResolver.swift:182).
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve the shell’s start directory as: the directory of `editor.currentFileURL` if a document is open, else the user’s home directory, else the current process directory. Because the shell is started once per `TerminalHostView`, changing tabs must not restart it — instead add a Shell header item (or context-menu item) “Go to Document Folder” that sends `cd <quoted path>` via `sendCommand`, which the existing OSC-7 handler will pick up to refresh the header path (Sources/Qnet/TerminalConsoleView.swift:551-566).
findings.acceptance_criteria: Launch Qnet.app from Finder with no document: the Shell header shows `~` and `pwd` prints the home directory. Open a saved network and use Go to Document Folder: `pwd` prints that folder and the header updates without restarting the shell (the scrollback and PID are unchanged).
findings.risk: Changing the initial directory changes relative-path behaviour for anything a user types; it also changes what `SolverRuntimeResolver`’s development-tree fallback would find if it ever consulted the shell’s cwd (it does not — it uses the process cwd, QnetGUIApp.swift:1424 — verify that stays true).

findings.title: Clean up wrapper scripts and make “re-run the last command” actually work
findings.user_impact: There is no Re-run. The only route is shell history: press ↑ and the user gets `bash "/tmp/BNET_run_<uuid>.sh"`. Pressing Return re-executes it, but the run is invisible to Qnet — `beginRun` was never called, so there is no status bar entry, no Stop button, no progress polling, and no Results record; the wrapper writes its pid and completion files to paths `finishRun` already deleted; and its opening `printf '\033[A\033[2K'` erases a line of the user’s own output. Meanwhile every wrapper script ever generated stays in TMPDIR — one file per run, forever.
findings.evidence: Script written and never removed: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5769-5771 and :7475-7478 (`BNET_run_<uuid>.sh`); `finishRun` removes done/pid/status/output/progress files but not the script (Sources/Qnet/TerminalModel.swift:718-737). Command typed into the shell (and therefore into shell history): Sources/Qnet/TerminalModel.swift:774-778, called at Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5836. Line erase: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5789.
findings.proposed_fix: (a) Remove the wrapper script in `finishRun` alongside the other coordination artifacts, and sweep stale `BNET_run_*.sh` for the current pid at launch. dimension: Output formatting consistency across every algorithm (decimal places, table shape, row labels, banners, units, failure presentation, station ordering)

findings.title: Normalize solver stdout at the terminal boundary so every algorithm honours outputDecimals
findings.user_impact:
Only 12 of the 22 run paths honour Settings ▸ Output Format ▸ Decimal places. Set decimals to 3, then run Exact Open Product Form and you get `Station s1 (fcfs): E[N]=0.66666667  throughput=1.2000000001`; run Exact Matrix-Analytic QBD and you get `QNET_QBD_METRIC_V1 metric=mean_level estimate=4.0000000000000018`; run SRBM MLMC and you get `L_1 = 4.0000 ± 0.0312`; run QNA and you get `E[Q_01]  4.000`. Four precisions, three table languages, one session, one network.

Full enumeration (method — line — solver — formatter — honours setting):
1 runSimulation 1648 fBNAsim singleMethodFormatCmd@1734 YES; 2 runGenericCTMC 1763 generic_ctmc/solver.py raw@1804 NO; 3 runFiniteDecomposition 1828 fbna_decomp.py raw@1877 NO; 4 runOpenProductForm 1902 product_form/solver.py raw@1941 NO; 5 runQBD 1965 qbd_solver.py --human raw@2007 NO; 6 runTruncatedCTMC 2032 truncated_ctmc.py --human raw@2082 NO; 7 runRegenerativeMonteCarlo 2134 regenerative_mc.py raw@2247 NO; 8 runAdaptiveLowRankBAR 2300 low_rank_bar.py raw@2343 NO; 9 runBARMomentBounds 2371 bar_bounds/solver.py raw@2414 NO; 10 runFiniteElement 2470 fBNAfm singleMethodFormatCmd@2515 YES; 11 runFiniteLP 2538 fBNAlp singleMethodFormatCmd@2592 YES; 12 runMultiClassSRBM 2657 mc_fem_gauss singleMethodFormatCmd@2702 YES; 13 runSpectralMethod 2739 fBNAsm singleMethodFormatCmd@2789 YES; 14 runComparison 2899 5 solvers buildComparisonAwk@3164 YES; 15 runSimulationInfinite 3209 jackson_sim singleMethodFormatCmd@3273 YES; 16 runSpectralMethodInfinite 3382 bnet singleMethodFormatCmd@3431 YES; 17 runQNA 3453 bna_qna singleMethodFormatCmd@3488 YES; 18 runRQNA 3505 bna_rqna singleMethodFormatCmd@3540 YES; 19 runSBD 3557 bna_sbd singleMethodFormatCmd@3600 YES; 20 runExactSim 3773 rbm_mlmc OWN awk %.4f@4157 NO; 21 runLinearProgram 4369 srbm_lp lpSummaryAwk %.4f@4519 + raw tee NO; 22 runComparisonInfinite 4568 5 solvers buildComparisonAwk@4808 YES. Plus runInfiniteTestSet/runFiniteTestSet/runSpectralConvergence (own awk at %.2f%%, :8045 and :8359) and the two report commands analyzeNetwork/showNetworkPrimitives.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5298 (the only read of appSettings.outputDecimals in the whole app), :5299, :5308; the ten non-honouring launches at :1804, :1877, :1941, :2007, :2082, :2247, :2343, :2414, :4157, :4519; AppSettings.swift:425; SettingsView.swift:2032 ("Affects only how Run Comparison and single-method tables print numbers")
findings.proposed_fix:
Add ONE formatting authority applied as a display-only filter in the shell pipeline, AFTER the tee. In `runScript` (QnetGUIApp.swift:5799) and `silentScript` (:7474) change `} 2>&1 | tee "<outputPath>"` to `} 2>&1 | tee "<outputPath>" | <numberFilter>`. `_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}` keeps referring to the brace group, so exit-status plumbing is unchanged. The tee file stays byte-for-byte full precision, so ResultOutputParser (which reads that file, TerminalModel.swift:697) and the CSV/JSON export keep every digit; only what the user SEES is rounded.

Build the filter as a perl one-liner emitted by a new `private func outputPrecisionFilter(decimals:) -> String` in QnetGUIApp.swift (perl is already an unconditional dependency, :5791). Requirements:
  • Unbuffered, CR-aware: `$|=1`, read fixed-size chunks, split records on /(?<=[\r\n])/, flush each. A line-oriented awk/sed filter would swallow every intermediate frame of withProgress/withSpinner (:5694-5737 write `\r`-terminated frames with no newline until the end) and destroy the progress UI. This is the biggest implementation risk.
  • Pass through verbatim any line matching /^QNET_[A-Z_]+_V1\b/ — QNET_QBD_METRIC_V1, QNET_NODE_METRIC_V1, QNET_MLMC_STATUS_V1, QNET_METHOD_FAILURE_V1, QNET_COMPARISON_STATUS_V1, QNET_SBD_STATUS_V1. Rounding them would corrupt stored results and break the integer-only regexes at ResultOutputParser.swift:94/106/114/121.
  • Skip ANSI escape runs /\e\[[0-?]*[ -\/]*[@-~]/ so cursor moves and colours pass untouched.
  • Rewrite only tokens matching /(?<![\w.])[+-]?(?:\d+\.\d+|\.\d+)(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?(?![\w.])/ — a number that ALREADY has a decimal point. Bare integers are left alone by construction, preserving counts, station indices, seeds, iteration counts, exit codes, cap values and `grid_n = 40`. The look-behind/look-ahead on [\w.] keeps `S1.2`, version `0.90.34` and paths `/tmp/BNET_run_3.4.sh` out.
  • Magnitude policy: if v == 0 or |v| >= 10^-decimals print `%.<d>f`; else `%.<max(1,d-1)>e`. Verified need: `awk 'function f(v){return sprintf("%.3f",v+0)} BEGIN{print f("1.5e-08"); print f("-0.0001")}'` prints `0.000` and `-0.000` today. Also normalize `-0.000…` to positive.
  • Column alignment: rewrite in place, pad/trim to the ORIGINAL token width when the replacement is shorter, so pre-aligned tables (lpSummaryAwk `%-16.4f`, MLMC `%10.4f`, showNetworkPrimitives `%10.5f`) do not shear.
  • Confidence intervals `x ± y` and `[low, high]` need no special case — both operands are independent decimal tokens.

Keep buildComparisonAwk's fmt7 using the same decimals so the awk tables are idempotent under the filter (`0.500` -> `0.500`); assert idempotence in a test.

Reject the alternative of passing `--decimals` to every solver: `grep -rho '%[-+ 0-9.*]*[fgeE]' infinite finite --include='*.c'` yields 43 distinct specifiers across 1,977 printf calls in 56 C files, and the Python solvers add 13 more (`:.6f`, `:.9g`, `:.17g`, `:.3e`, …). That is ~23 output writers, each with its own argparse/getopt surface, unit tests, examples, README and validation/algo_review note. It multiplies the change surface by 20 and delivers nothing the boundary filter does not, because display precision is a GUI preference, not a solver property.
findings.acceptance_criteria: With Decimal places = 3, run each of the 22 methods on a network it supports and confirm: every decimal number in the Interactive Shell shows exactly 3 fraction digits, or scientific with 2 significant digits when |v| < 1e-3; no bare integer gained a decimal point (station indices, `Complete empty-to-empty cycles: 4812`, `Selected total cap: 24`, iteration counts, seeds, exit codes); every `QNET_*_V1` line is byte-identical to what the solver emitted; the progress bar and spinner still animate frame by frame; the tee'd run-output file still holds the solver's original digits. Repeat at 0 and 9. validation/gui_runtime_contracts.sh, validation/design_lint.sh and `swift build` pass; AppVersion stays 0.90.34.
findings.risk: CR-buffering: a naive line filter kills withProgress/withSpinner (:5694-5737). If the filter is inserted BEFORE the tee, ResultOutputParser (:140) and the CSV export (ResultsWorkspace.swift:695) silently start recording rounded values — a data-integrity regression worse than the bug. `PIPESTATUS[0]` must keep pointing at the brace group, so add the filter as a second pipe stage, never wrap the group. gui_runtime_contracts.sh greps exact strings in QnetGUIApp.swift including the cleanup/trap region; reread validation/gui_runtime_contracts.sh:20-45 before editing runScript/silentScript.

findings.title: Stop discarding solver confidence intervals in every table
findings.user_impact: Every simulator emits a half-width beside its estimate, buildComparisonAwk parses it into `ci_rh`/`ci_gm`/`ci_sj`/`ci_xc`/`ci_ex`, and then never reads those arrays again. A 50-replication Monte Carlo — the whole point of which is the error bar — prints a bare number with a %-delta and no indication of sampling error. The Results pane is equally blank: ResultOutputParser's uncertainty capture group `(?:\s+\((number)\))?` can never fire on a comparison table, because the only parenthesised token there is `(+1.2%)` and `percentDelta` strips it first. `ResultUncertainty` is therefore nil for all 12 awk-formatted methods and the Results pane's evidence column shows "—" for a simulation.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:5277-5281 (ci_rh/ci_gm/ci_sj/ci_xc/ci_ex assigned) — grepping those names over the whole file returns only those five lines; they are never read in the END block at :5313-5447. Solvers that DO emit half-widths: finite/fBNAsim/stats.c:226, :253, :275, :284, :309, :327 (`%.6f\t(%.6f)`); infinite/BNAsim/jackson_sim.c:2003, :2016, :2035, :2049 (`%f\t(%.4f)`). Parser side: ResultOutputParser.swift:26-28 (percentDelta), :30 and :34 (the uncertainty group that can no longer match), :167 and :185 (`uncertaintyText: groups[safe: 4]`)
