Put the `± half` BEFORE the `(+x.x%)` delta so `percentDelta` stripping still leaves `value ± half` intact for `stationRow`/`expectationRow`. Then extend ResultOutputParser.swift:30 and :34 so the optional uncertainty group accepts `±\s*(number)` in addition to the legacy `\((number)\)` form — `convertedQueueRow` at :42 already has that shape, so reuse it. Keep the parenthesised alternative so raw solver output pasted into the terminal still parses. Where a method has no CI (every analytical solver) print nothing extra; a fabricated ± on a deterministic method is worse than none. Fixing this also fixes the Results pane and CSV export for free, since both read `measurement.uncertainty` (ResultsWorkspace.swift:1917-1925, :744-751).

Editing the two regexes at ResultOutputParser.swift:30/:34 is a validation-contract change: validation/result_output_parser/ compiles that one real file against stubs.swift, so the stub must not need to grow.

Verified against the actual fmt7 body: `awk 'function f(v){return sprintf("%.3f",v+0)} BEGIN{print f("1.5e-08"); print f("-0.0001")}'` prints `0.000` and `-0.000`.

Normalize an all-zero result carrying a leading minus to the positive spelling. Column widths adapt automatically because the width pass at :5433 measures the built strings. Document the rule once — in the Settings footnote (SettingsView.swift:2032) and in the DS.Number doc comment — so the switch to scientific notation is a stated behaviour rather than a surprise.

With decimals = 6 and a value of 0.5 the cell still renders `0.500000` (no regression for ordinary magnitudes). The `(+x.x%)` delta still suppresses itself when the reference rounds to zero.

Change both halves together. Mixed fixed/scientific cells in one column make decimal-point alignment impossible — accept right-alignment (next finding) as the reconciliation.

findings.title: The Results pane and the in-app readouts use three more precision rules, none of them outputDecimals

  • Derived MODEL readouts (inspector μ/SCV/ρ previews, routing totals, flag-bar predictions) → keep `DS.Number.readoutDigits = 5` significant digits. These describe the network being edited, not a solver result, and a decimal-places rule is wrong for a probability and a rate in the same column.

findings.title: Give the empty canvas a real first-run surface instead of one non-interactive sentence
findings.user_impact: First launch shows five panes at once and an empty canvas whose entire guidance is two lines of grey text that cannot be clicked: "Press S, then click to place a station. / Or open an example from File ▸ Open Example… (⇧⌘O)". There is no onboarding state anywhere in the app. At the 1000 × 720 minimum window the canvas gets roughly 496 × 320 pt — under a third of the window — while the Tools, Inspector, Status, Shell and AI panes take the rest. A new user's first impression is a crowded IDE with a small grey box in the middle.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasOverlays.swift:161-171 `CanvasEmptyHint` — a `DSEmptyState` with no `actionTitle`/`action` and `.allowsHitTesting(false)` at :169. `grep -rin 'firstRun\|firstLaunch\|welcome\|onboard\|hasSeen\|tutorial' Sources/Qnet/*.swift` returns nothing but the unrelated `selectFirstRunIfNeeded` in ResultsWorkspace. Default pane visibility: Sources/Qnet/AppSettings.swift:135-139, :150 — palette, status, shell, inspector and AI all `true` (only results is `false`). Minimum widths that must all fit inside `Window.mainMinWidth = 1000` (DesignSystem.swift:1166): palettePaneMinWidth 152 + canvasPaneMinWidth 496 + rightColumnMinWidth 288 = 936 in the top row; heights: canvasRowMinHeight 320 + bottomRowMinHeight 192 + tabBarHeight 32 + statusBarHeight 24 = 568 inside mainMinHeight 720 (DesignSystem.swift:1142-1151, :931-933, :1167). DSEmptyState already supports one action button (DSEmptyState.swift:29-31, :80-92) — it is simply not used here.
findings.proposed_fix: Two parts, both presentation-only. (a) Make the canvas empty state actionable: pass `actionTitle: "Open an Example…"` with a `keyboardShortcut` and the existing Open Example command, and drop the blanket `.allowsHitTesting(false)` (DSEmptyState already scopes hit-testing so the text block stays transparent to canvas gestures — DSEmptyState.swift:73/:79). Extend DSEmptyState to take a primary plus up to two secondary actions so the canvas can offer "Open an Example…", "Insert a Tandem Queue" and "Show the Tools Pane". (b) Add a `first.launch.seen` @AppStorage flag in AppSettings and, on a genuinely first launch only, open with the Results, AI and Inspector panes hidden so the canvas gets the window. NOTE: the canvas archetype / drag-and-drop work itself belongs to the canvas-UX reviewer — this finding is the empty state and the opening composition, not the palette content.
findings.acceptance_criteria: On a clean UserDefaults domain, first launch shows the canvas occupying at least half the window width with actionable buttons in the empty state; clicking "Open an Example…" opens the example picker; clicking anywhere else on the empty canvas still places a node / starts a marquee exactly as today. A second launch restores the user's own pane layout and never shows the first-run composition again. `Qnet --ds-gallery` renders the multi-action DSEmptyState. The lint's empty-state Title Case check still passes.
findings.risk: The empty state currently disables hit-testing wholesale to keep canvas gestures working — re-enabling it for the buttons must not swallow clicks meant for the canvas; test placing a node directly under the button row. The first-launch pane override must write through the same @AppStorage keys the View ▸ Panes menu uses, or the menu checkmarks will disagree with what is on screen.

findings.title: Retire the ad-hoc font weights applied to DS tokens at seven call sites
findings.user_impact: Seven places bolt a weight onto a DS font token, producing faces that exist nowhere in the scale: an 11-pt BOLD in the flag-bar popover where every other emphasised 11-pt in the app is semibold, plus a medium 12-pt tab title, medium 10-pt status-bar glyphs and a bare `.fontWeight(.medium)` inherited onto a status-bar segment. The scale stops being one thing, which is the exact failure the DS's rule 1 exists to prevent.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/FlagBarView.swift:108 `.font(DS.Font.subheadline.bold())` — the token for that is `DS.Font.chromeEmphasis` (subheadline.semibold, DesignSystem.swift:1307); Sources/Qnet/ContentView.swift:724 `DS.Font.label.weight(.medium)`, :848/:889/:912 `DS.Font.caption.weight(.medium)`, :851 a bare `.fontWeight(.medium)`; Sources/Qnet/DSBadge.swift:86 and :264 `DS.Font.numberCaption.weight(.bold)`. validation/design_lint.sh:1-90 checks `.font(.system(size:` and bare text styles but has no rule for a weight modifier chained onto a DS token, so all seven pass today.
findings.proposed_fix: For each site pick the existing token (`chromeEmphasis` for FlagBarView:108; `labelEmphasis` for ContentView:724) or add one named token to DS.Font in DesignSystem.swift for the two genuinely new faces — a `captionEmphasis` (10-pt medium, for the three status-bar glyph sites) and a `numberCaptionEmphasis` (10-pt bold digits, for DSBadge's count capsule). Then add a lint rule matching `DS\.Font\.[A-Za-z]+\.(bold|italic|weight)\(` and a bare `\.fontWeight\(` outside DesignSystem.swift.
findings.acceptance_criteria: `grep -rnE 'DS\.Font\.[A-Za-z]+\.(bold|italic|weight)\(|\.fontWeight\(' Sources/Qnet/*.swift` returns hits only in DesignSystem.swift; the new lint rule fails on a reintroduced site; the type-scale section of `Qnet --ds-gallery` renders any newly added token.
findings.risk: Low. FlagBarView:108 goes from bold to semibold — a deliberate, visible change; confirm in the gallery that the popover heading still reads as a heading against the callout body beneath it.

findings.title: Replace the Unicode sort arrows in the Results header with DS.Symbol tokens
findings.user_impact: The Results table's sort indicator is a raw "↑"/"↓" character in the body font — the only glyph in the app not drawn from the SF Symbol vocabulary. It renders at a different weight and optical size from every other icon on the same screen, and being a text character it sits on the text baseline rather than centred with the header label.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/ResultsWorkspace.swift:1199-1202 `Text(sortAscending ? "↑" : "↓")`. `DS.Symbol` (Sources/Qnet/DesignSystem.swift:1592-1731) has `stepPrevious`/`stepNext` (chevron.up/down) but no sort-direction pair. The lint cannot catch this: validation/design_lint.sh:210-214 only matches a literal after `systemImage:`/`systemName:`, and its generated-alternation rule at :216-238 matches SF Symbol NAMES, not Unicode characters.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `sortAscending` / `sortDescending` to DS.Symbol in DesignSystem.swift with a comment naming them as the table-sort indicator (chevron.up/down to match the app's existing vertical-step pair, or arrow.up/down if sort should read distinctly), and draw them as `Image(systemName:)` sized to `DS.Font.tableHeader` so they sit with the label. Extend the lint's raw-symbol rule with a small alternation of arrow characters (↑ ↓ ▲ ▼) inside double-quoted strings outside DesignSystem.swift.
findings.acceptance_criteria: The sort indicator is an SF Symbol vertically centred with its column heading; `grep -n '"↑"' Sources/Qnet/*.swift` returns nothing; the lint rejects a reintroduced Unicode arrow in a display string. Existing prose that legitimately uses arrows (the "S1 → S2" link labels, the "▸" menu-path convention the lint already enforces) is unaffected.
findings.risk: The lint's menu-path rule already governs "→" vs "▸" (validation/design_lint.sh header line 51) and `editor.displayLabel(for: link)` builds "S1 → S2" strings — scope the new arrow rule to ↑/↓/▲/▼ only, or it will collide.

findings.title: Give Results measurement rows a hover state — they are the only clickable surface in the app without one
findings.user_impact: Every measurement row in the Results table is clickable (it selects the station on the canvas) but gives no hover feedback, so nothing tells the user the rows are live. Every other clickable surface in the window — tool buttons, icon buttons, tabs, pills, palette rows, the glossary "?" — lifts under the pointer with the shared DS wash.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/ResultsWorkspace.swift:1877-1901 — `.contentShape(Rectangle()).onTapGesture(perform: action)` with `.background(selected ? DS.Color.selectionFill(a11y.contrast) : Color.clear)` and no `onHover`. The view already declares `@DSAccessibility private var a11y` at :1881, so the adaptive hover token is one line away. The pattern it should match: Sources/Qnet/DSButtons.swift:198-206 and :252-258. `grep -c onHover Sources/Qnet/ResultsWorkspace.swift` returns 0.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `@State private var isHovering = false` and `.onHover { withAnimation(a11y.animation(DS.Motion.quick)) { isHovering = $0 } }`, and make the background `selected ? DS.Color.selectionFill(a11y.contrast) : (isHovering ? DS.Color.hoverFill(a11y.contrast) : .clear)` — exactly the ordering DSToolbarButtonBody uses. Do the same for the comparison grid's rows if they are clickable.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Hovering a measurement row shows the same wash a hovered palette row shows; the wash steps up under Increase Contrast; a selected row keeps the selection wash while hovered. `validation/design_lint.sh` passes.
findings.risk: Low. Per-row hover means one @State per row; the rows are already individual views (`ResultsMeasurementRow`), so there is no new allocation pattern.

findings.title: Move the Results detail pane's three off-scale typographic habits back onto the DS scale
findings.user_impact: The Results detail pane invents its own micro-typography: ALL-CAPS field labels that appear nowhere else in the app, and three content labels drawn in the faintest ink the design system has, which the DS's own doc comment reserves for placeholders and decorative glyphs. "3 measurements" — a fact the user needs — is drawn in the same grey as an em-dash placeholder.
findings.evidence: All-caps: Sources/Qnet/ResultsWorkspace.swift:1634 and :1751 `Text(label.uppercased())` — `grep -rn '\.uppercased()' Sources/Qnet/*.swift` shows these are the app's only two all-caps UI labels (the others, KeyboardShortcutReference.swift:240 and StatusLog.swift:172, are exported text files, and there is no `.textCase(` anywhere). Tertiary-as-content: ResultsWorkspace.swift:1542 ("N measurements"), :1636 and :1753 (the field labels above). The rule being broken: Sources/Qnet/DesignSystem.swift:372-373 "**placeholders, em-dash empties and decorative glyphs only**. Never content." and :143-148 in the adoption guide. By contrast the same file's legitimate tertiary uses are correct — em-dashes at NodeInspectorSections.swift:1152-1154 and chevrons at :1024.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace both `Text(label.uppercased())` with sentence-case labels in `DS.Font.caption` + `DS.Color.textSecondary`, matching the summary/evidence pattern the inspectors already use; change :1542's "N measurements" to `DS.Color.textSecondary`. If a smaller-than-secondary label style is genuinely wanted for a summary grid, add ONE token for it to DesignSystem.swift rather than reaching for tertiary.
findings.acceptance_criteria: `grep -n 'uppercased()' Sources/Qnet/ResultsWorkspace.swift` returns nothing; the run-summary and evidence field labels read "Started", "Elapsed" in the same case and colour as the inspectors' row labels; no `DS.Color.textTertiary` in ResultsWorkspace carries text a user must read. `validation/design_lint.sh` and `validation/ds_contrast.swift` pass.
findings.risk: Very low, presentation only. Worth confirming VoiceOver no longer spells the labels out letter-by-letter.

findings.title: Extend the glossary to the results and solver vocabulary, and stop leaking solver binary names into Settings tooltips
findings.user_impact: The design system's jargon rule covers Greek symbols and stops there. The words a MATLAB user actually meets first — SRBM, CTMC, QNA, MLMC, QBD, BAR, "sojourn", "Mean workload" — appear in Settings pane titles, alert titles and the Results table with no "?" anywhere and no entry in DS.Glossary. And the Settings sidebar's row tooltips read "rbm_mlmc accuracy, overrides and reproducibility" and "bna_fm quadrature and mesh" — raw executable filenames in mixed snake_case and camelCase, spoken aloud by VoiceOver as the row's hint. On the canvas a buffer node's label reads "b=5" and its tooltip never explains what b is, even though DS.Glossary.bufferSize already exists.
findings.evidence: Missing entries: `DS.Glossary` (Sources/Qnet/DesignSystem.swift:1515-1571) has 35 entries covering λ μ ρ Γ SCV c BAS and solver parameters, and none for SRBM / CTMC / QNA / RQNA / MLMC / QBD / BAR / sojourn. Where they surface unexplained: Sources/Qnet/SettingsView.swift:39 and :56 (pane titled "SRBM MLMC"); Sources/Qnet/QnetGUIApp.swift:1770 "Exact CTMC Runtime Unavailable", :2035, :2060, :2392 "BAR Moment Bounds Are Not Applicable", :2491 "SRBM Export Failed"; Sources/Qnet/ResultOutputParser.swift:164 "Mean sojourn time", :181-182 "Mean workload" / "Mean number in system". Binary names in tooltips: Sources/Qnet/SettingsView.swift:104-108 (`summary`, rendered as `.help(tab.summary)` at :248 and as the accessibility hint at :251-252). The buffer gap: Sources/Qnet/NetworkCanvasLayers.swift:565 `return "b=\(node.bufferSize)"` while `tooltipDescription` at :631-640 appends glossary text only for `.source` and `.station`, never `.buffer`, although `DS.Glossary.bufferSize` exists at DesignSystem.swift:1529.
findings.proposed_fix: (a) Add glossary entries for srbm, ctmc, qna, mlmc, qbd, bar, sojourn and workload to DS.Glossary. (b) Wire them: `DSHelpButton`/`DSGlossaryButton` on the Settings pane titles that carry an acronym, and a `help:` on the Results Metric column heading (the DS documents `help:` on a table column heading as the sanctioned form, DesignSystem.swift:311-313). (c) Rewrite the five Settings `summary` strings in human terms ("Run length, parallelism and blocking for discrete-event simulation") and move the binary name, if worth keeping, into the pane body. (d) Add `case .buffer: lines.append(DS.Glossary.bufferSize)` to NetworkCanvasLayers.swift's `tooltipDescription` switch and spell the canvas label "buffer 5" rather than "b=5" when the zoom allows.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Hovering the Settings sidebar rows shows no executable filename; the SRBM MLMC pane carries a "?" that defines both acronyms; the Results Metric column heading carries a `help:` defining sojourn time and workload; hovering a buffer node explains what b is. `validation/design_lint.sh` passes, including its rule that every `DS.Glossary` entry is referenced and that `DS.Glossary.all` names every one of them.
findings.risk: The lint fails the build if a new `static let` in DS.Glossary is not added to `DS.Glossary.all` AND not referenced by a view — add entry, list and call site in the same change. `SettingsGlossaryAudit`'s runtime membership check depends on `all` being complete. Changing the canvas label from "b=5" widens the node label block — check it against `NodeOutline.labelBlockWidth` (NetworkCanvasLayers.swift:535) at low zoom.

findings.title: Tint the Tools palette glyphs with the node-kind colours the canvas already uses
findings.user_impact: The Tools pane draws all eight tool glyphs in the same primary ink, so nothing connects "Station" in the palette to the blue circle it produces on the canvas, or "Source" to the green diamond. The mapping has to be learned by trial. The app already owns the colour and already uses it for exactly this purpose in the Inspector header.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/ToolPaletteView.swift:63-66 — `Image(systemName: tool.systemImage).font(DS.Font.control)` with no `foregroundStyle`, so it inherits `DS.Color.textPrimary` from DSPaletteButtonStyle (DSButtons.swift:262). The token that should be there: `DS.Color.nodeTint(for:)` at Sources/Qnet/DesignSystem.swift:617-624, already used the right way at Sources/Qnet/InspectorPaneView.swift:83 for the header's node-kind glyph.
findings.proposed_fix: Where `EditorTool` maps to a `NodeKind` (station, buffer, source, sink), apply `.foregroundStyle(DS.Color.nodeTint(for: kind))` to the palette glyph; leave the non-node tools (select, marquee, hand, link) on `DS.Color.textPrimary`. Check the tinted glyph against the selection wash in both appearances — `nodeTint` returns the raw signal colours, which are FILL tokens; at `DS.Font.control` (13 pt) they are large enough to be legal as glyphs, but switch to the `*Text` variants if they read poorly (DesignSystem.swift:439-441).
findings.acceptance_criteria: The Station, Buffer, Source and Sink palette glyphs carry the same tint as their node headers in the Inspector and their fills on the canvas; the four non-node tools are unchanged; contrast is acceptable on the selection wash in light and dark (eyeball in `Qnet --ds-gallery`'s palette-button specimen). `validation/design_lint.sh` passes — in particular its "no signal colour as ink" rule, which matches `foregroundStyle([^)]*DS\.Color\.(success|warning|danger|info)`; `nodeTint(for:)` is an indirection so it passes, but if the glyphs read poorly switch to the *Text variants rather than defeating the rule.
findings.risk: `nodeTint` returns `info`/`bufferTint`/`success`/`danger` — the signal colours. Colouring a palette row green or red risks reading as "this tool is OK / broken". Confirm with the canvas side by side; if it reads as status rather than kind, use a smaller coloured swatch beside the glyph instead.

findings.title: Render the ten DS components the gallery currently omits, so the reference matches its own claim
findings.user_impact: DesignSystem.swift tells every future builder that `Qnet --ds-gallery` shows "every token and every DS component". Ten do not appear, including DSPaletteButtonStyle (the style behind the entire Tools pane), DSInspectorRow (the row every field in both inspectors is built from) and DSGlossaryButton/DSHelpButton (the app's whole jargon affordance). A reference with silent holes is where the next duplicate component gets written.
findings.evidence: Sources/Qnet/DesignSystem.swift:22-23 "`Qnet --ds-gallery`  opens DSGallery.swift: every token and every DS component rendered side by side". Cross-referencing every `struct DS*` declared in Sources/Qnet/DS*.swift against occurrences in Sources/Qnet/DSGallery.swift gives zero hits for: DSGlossaryButton, DSGlossarySlot, DSHelpButton, DSInspectorRow, DSInspectorRowPlaceholder, DSMenuPicker, DSPaletteButtonStyle, DSRowLabel, DSSheetGlyph, DSSheetMissingTarget.
findings.proposed_fix: Add one specimen row per missing component to DSGallery.swift following the file's existing `Specimen(name:detail:)` pattern — in particular a palette-button row in idle/hover/pressed/selected/disabled beside the existing DSIconButton row, a DSInspectorRow in all four DSRowLayouts beside the existing DSNumericField specimens, and a DSGlossaryButton + DSGlossarySlot pair showing the reserved-column alignment that DesignSystem.swift:953-957 describes only in prose. If a component is deliberately not worth a specimen (DSSheetMissingTarget), say so in the gallery header rather than leaving the claim unqualified.
findings.acceptance_criteria: For every `struct DS…: View` or `: ButtonStyle` declared in Sources/Qnet/DS*.swift, either its name appears in DSGallery.swift or the gallery header names it as a deliberate omission with a reason. `Qnet --ds-gallery` renders each new specimen in all three columns without clipping in the Accessibility 1 column. `validation/design_lint.sh` passes (the gallery is not exempt from the token rules).
findings.risk: The gallery is compiled into the release binary on purpose (DSGallery.swift:49-53) — keep the additions cheap and hold no app state. Its frame-literal history means the lint watches this file closely; use the DS.Layout.gallerySpecimen* tokens for every new box.
